title.zh: 卷239 列傳二十六 沈文奎 李栖凤 马国柱 丁文盛 祝世昌
title.en: Volume 239 Biographies 26: Shen Wenkui, Li Qifeng, Ma Guozhu, Ding Wensheng, Zhu Shichang
title.raw: 卷239 列傳二十六 沈文奎 李栖凤 马国柱 丁文盛 祝世昌

sentences.zh: 沈文奎，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Shen Wenkui was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenkui was a native of Kuaiji, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少寄育外家王氏，因其姓。

translations.literal: In youth he was fostered and raised in the household of his maternal kin the Wang family and took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was raised by his mother's family, the Wangs, and bore their surname.

sentences.zh: 年二十，為明諸生，北遊遵化。

translations.literal: At age twenty he became a licentiate under the Ming and traveled north to Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he qualified as a Ming licentiate and went north to Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，太宗伐明，下遵化，文奎降。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong, the Taizong attacked the Ming, took Zunhua, and Wenkui surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancong (1629), Hong Taiji campaigned against the Ming, captured Zunhua, and Wenkui submitted.

sentences.zh: 從貝勒豪格以歸，命值文館。

translations.literal: He returned with Prince Hoge and was ordered to serve in the Literary Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He returned with Prince Hoge and was assigned to the Literary Institute.

sentences.zh: 漢軍旗制定，隸鑲白旗。

translations.literal: When the Han military banners were established, he was enrolled in the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: After the Han banners were organized, he was placed in the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，上自將伐察哈爾，因略宣府邊外。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year, the sovereign personally led a campaign against the Chahar and, on the way, raided beyond the borders of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year, the khan led an expedition against the Chahar and swept the country beyond Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 明文武大吏請盟，上還師。

translations.literal: Ming civil and military grandees requested a treaty alliance, and the sovereign withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ming officials civil and military sued for peace, and the khan withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 八月丁卯，召文奎及同值文館諸生孫應時、江雲深入宮賜饌，命策和議成否。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day of the eighth month, Wenkui and his fellow Literary Institute students Sun Yingshi and Jiang Yunshen were summoned into the palace, given a feast, and ordered to deliberate whether peace talks could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingmao day in the eighth month, Wenkui and fellow institute scholars Sun Yingshi and Jiang Yunshen were called to court, entertained at a banquet, and asked whether a negotiated peace was feasible.

sentences.zh: 文奎等皆言明政日紊，中原盜賊蜂起，民困於離亂。

translations.literal: Wenkui and the others all said that Ming government grew daily more disorderly, bandits swarmed in the Central Plain, and the people were afflicted by separation and turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkui and the others agreed that Ming rule was collapsing, rebels were rising across the heartland, and the people were worn down by chaos and displacement.

sentences.zh: 勸上宣布仁義，用賢養民，乘時吊伐。

translations.literal: They urged the sovereign to proclaim benevolence and righteousness, employ the worthy and nurture the people, and take advantage of the moment to succor the suffering and punish the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: They urged him to proclaim humane rule, appoint able men, care for the people, and seize the moment for a punitive campaign in the name of relieving distress.

sentences.zh: 文奎等退，各具疏陳所見。

translations.literal: Wenkui and the others withdrew, and each submitted a memorial setting forth his views.
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawing, Wenkui and the others each memorialized the throne with their views.

sentences.zh: 文奎疏言：「先帝用兵之初，勢若破竹，蓋以執北關之釁，名正言順。

translations.literal: Wenkui memorialized, saying: "At the beginning of the late emperor's use of arms, his momentum was like splitting bamboo, because he seized upon the provocation at the northern passes—his cause was righteous and his words accorded with right.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkui wrote: "When the late khan first took the field, his armies swept forward like bamboo split along the grain, for he held the Ming to blame for the incident at the northern passes—his cause was just and his title to act unimpeachable.

sentences.zh: 其後多疑好殺，百姓離心，皆曰利我子女玉帛耳。

translations.literal: Afterward he grew suspicious and fond of killing; the common people turned their hearts away, all saying that he sought only our children, silk, and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Later he grew suspicious and bloodthirsty, and the people turned against him, saying his aim was only to seize their sons and daughters, silk, and treasure.

sentences.zh: 上寬仁大度，推心置人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is magnanimous and broad-minded, placing your heart in others.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is generous and open-handed, trusting others with a full heart.

sentences.zh: 今師次宣、大，長驅而入，誰復敢當？

translations.literal: Now the army halts at Xuan and Datong; if it drives straight in, who will dare stand in its way?
translations.idiomatic: Your army now stands at Xuanfu and Datong; a straight advance—who could withstand it?

sentences.zh: 乃以片言之故，卷甲休兵。

translations.literal: Yet for the sake of a few words you have rolled up your armor and halted the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for a few words of negotiation you have sheathed your armies and stopped the campaign.

sentences.zh: 大信已著，宜乘時遣使，略遜其辭，以踐張家口之約。

translations.literal: Great faith is already manifest; you should seize the moment to send envoys, slightly softening your language, to fulfill the agreement at Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Your good faith is already plain; send envoys at once, temper your tone a little, and honor the pact made at Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 夫不利人之危，仁也；

translations.literal: Not to take advantage of another's peril is benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: To refuse profit from another's danger is benevolence;

sentences.zh: 不乘人之亂，勇也；

translations.literal: not to exploit another's disorder is courage;
translations.idiomatic: to forgo striking amid another's chaos is courage;

sentences.zh: 不失舊約，信也：一舉而三美歸焉。

translations.literal: not to break the old covenant is faithfulness: in one act the three virtues are gathered.
translations.idiomatic: and to keep the old agreement is trustworthiness—in a single gesture you gain all three virtues.

sentences.zh: 或謂南朝首吝王封，次論地土人民，和必不成。

translations.literal: Some say the Southern Court will first be stingy with enfeoffment as king, next haggle over territory and people, and peace will surely fail.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the Ming will first refuse a royal enfeoffment, then dispute land and subjects, so peace cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 臣謂和否不在南朝，在上意定不定耳。

translations.literal: Your servant says whether peace succeeds lies not with the Southern Court but with whether Your Majesty's mind is settled.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that peace does not depend on the Ming but on whether Your Majesty's own resolve is firm.

sentences.zh: 且和而成，我坐收其利，以待天時；

translations.literal: Moreover, if peace is achieved, we sit and reap the benefit while awaiting Heaven's season;
translations.idiomatic: If peace is made, we can reap the advantage at leisure and wait for Heaven's moment;

sentences.zh: 和而不成，或薊鎮，或宣、大，或山海，乘時深入，誕告於眾曰：'幽、燕本金故地，陵墓在房山，吾第复吾故疆耳。

translations.literal: if peace fails, whether through Jizhen, Xuan and Datong, or Shanhai Pass, advance deep at the opportune moment and openly announce to the masses: 'Youzhou and Yan were originally Jin territory; the imperial tombs are at Fangshan—we seek only to recover our former borders.'
translations.idiomatic: if it fails, strike through Jizhen, Xuan-Datong, or Shanhaiguan when the moment is ripe, and proclaim to all: 'Youzhou and Yan are our Jin homeland; our ancestral tombs stand at Fangshan—we mean only to restore our old domain.'

sentences.zh: '師行毋殺人，毋劫掠，則彼民必怨其君之不和，而信我無他志矣。

translations.literal: Let the army march without killing people or plundering, and their people will surely resent their ruler for refusing peace and believe that we have no other designs.
translations.idiomatic: March without killing or looting, and their people will blame their ruler for rejecting peace and trust that we have no further ambitions.

sentences.zh: 大凌河降夷，上赦之刀斧之下，復加以恩育，其所以去者，皆父母妻子牽其念耳。

translations.literal: The surrendered tribesmen of Dalinghe—Your Majesty spared them beneath the axe and again showed them nurturing grace; the reason they fled was only that parents, wives, and children drew their thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen who surrendered at Dalinghe—you spared them from execution and treated them kindly; they fled only because parents, wives, and children held their hearts.

sentences.zh: 文王王政，罪不及孥。

translations.literal: In King Wen's royal government, guilt did not extend to wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Wen's rule, punishment did not reach a man's family.

sentences.zh: 執殺逃亡，已正國法。

translations.literal: To seize and execute fugitives already rectifies the law of the state.
translations.idiomatic: To arrest and execute deserters is already to uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 豈可因兄及弟，因父及子？

translations.literal: How can one implicate brothers because of an elder brother, or sons because of a father?
translations.idiomatic: How can guilt pass from brother to brother, or from father to son?

sentences.zh: 以一降夷而使眾降夷自危，且使凡自大凌河降者人人坐疑，非上明白宣諭，上下暌違，終不能釋也。

translations.literal: Because of one surrendered tribesman to make all surrendered tribesmen feel endangered, and to make everyone who surrendered from Dalinghe sit under suspicion—unless Your Majesty clearly proclaims and instructs, ruler and subjects will remain estranged and the matter can never be resolved.
translations.idiomatic: To punish one surrendered tribesman is to put all of them in fear and cast suspicion on every man who came over from Dalinghe; unless Your Majesty issues a clear proclamation, mistrust between court and subjects will never lift.

sentences.zh: 我國衣冠無制，貪而富者，即氓隸，冠裳埒王侯；

translations.literal: In our state dress and caps are unregulated: the greedy who grow rich, though mere commoners, wear robes rivaling princes and marquises;
translations.idiomatic: Our realm has no fixed dress code: a greedy commoner who grows rich may dress like a prince;

sentences.zh: 清而貧者，即高官，服飾同僕從。

translations.literal: the upright who are poor, though high officials, dress like servants.
translations.idiomatic: while an upright but poor high official may look no better than a servant.

sentences.zh: 乞上獨斷，定衣冠之制，使主權尊，民志定，賢愚僉奮，國日以強。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to decide alone, fix regulations for dress and caps, make sovereign authority honored, settle the people's will, stir worthy and simple alike to exert themselves, and the state will grow stronger day by day."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decree a proper dress code so that royal authority is honored, the people's minds are settled, all alike are stirred to effort, and the state grows stronger daily."

translations.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: (Wenkui's memorial closed.)

sentences.zh: 雲深疏言：「南朝未能決和，宜倍道徑取山海。

translations.literal: Yunshen memorialized, saying: "The Southern Court cannot decide on peace; you should march at double speed straight to take Shanhai Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yunshen wrote: "Since the Ming cannot settle on peace, march at forced pace and seize Shanhaiguan directly.

sentences.zh: 山海既破，八城折入於我，再與畫界議好，和乃可定。」

translations.literal: Once Shanhai is broken, the eight cities will fold into our possession; then negotiate boundaries and peace, and alliance can be fixed."
translations.idiomatic: Once Shanhaiguan falls, the eight garrison towns will come over to us; then draw borders and negotiate peace on terms we can fix."

translations.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: (Jiang Yunshen's memorial closed.)

sentences.zh: 應時疏言：「用兵當先足民。

translations.literal: Yingshi memorialized, saying: "In employing troops one must first make the people sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yingshi wrote: "Before waging war, the people must first be provided for.

sentences.zh: 年來國用不舒，今歲又被災，十室九空，宜乘時究方略，轉虛為盈，此宜急議者也。

translations.literal: In recent years state revenue has not flowed freely; this year disaster struck again—nine houses in ten stand empty. You should seize the moment to study measures, turn emptiness into fullness; this deserves urgent deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: State finances have been strained for years, and fresh disasters have left nine homes in ten empty; study remedies now and turn deficit into surplus—this should be debated at once.

sentences.zh: 八門徵稅，正稅外有羨銀，稅一兩非增三四分不收，朘削窮民脂血，此宜嚴覈者也。

translations.literal: At the eight gates taxes are levied; beyond the regular tax there is surplus silver—for one tael of tax they will not collect unless three or four fen more are added, paring away the poor people's very blood and fat; this should be strictly audited.
translations.idiomatic: At the eight gates collectors take surcharges on top of the regular levy, refusing a single tael unless three or four fen extra are added, bleeding the poor dry—this calls for strict audit.

sentences.zh: 六部公廨已畢工，人人當盡心力為上治事，否則不惟負上，抑且負此巨室，此宜申飭者也。

translations.literal: The public offices of the Six Ministries are already completed; every man should devote heart and strength to governing affairs for Your Majesty—otherwise he fails not only Your Majesty but also this great establishment; this should be sternly enjoined.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Ministries' offices are finished; every official should serve the throne with full devotion, or he betrays both the sovereign and the state itself—this deserves a stern order.

sentences.zh: 大凌河新夷，固自取滅亡，然邊防嚴則逋逃何自越，此亦宜申飭者也。」

translations.literal: The new tribesmen of Dalinghe indeed brought ruin on themselves, yet if frontier defense is strict, how can fugitives cross over of themselves? This too should be sternly enjoined."
translations.idiomatic: The new tribesmen from Dalinghe courted their own ruin, yet with strict frontier defense fugitives could not slip across—this too should be ordered."

translations.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: (Sun Yingshi's memorial closed.)

sentences.zh: 是歲近明邊蒙古部民逃入沙河堡，明兵索還。

translations.literal: That year Mongol tribesmen near the Ming border fled into Shahe Fort; Ming troops demanded their return.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mongol tribesmen along the Ming frontier fled into Shahe Fort, and Ming forces demanded them back.

sentences.zh: 文奎、應時疏中曰「降夷」，曰「新夷」，蓋謂是也。

translations.literal: In the memorials of Wenkui and Yingshi they speak of "surrendered tribesmen" and "new tribesmen"—this is what they meant.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkui and Yingshi's memorials speak of "surrendered tribesmen" and "new tribesmen"—they referred to this affair.

sentences.zh: 九月，文奎复疏言：「臣自入國後，見上封事者多矣，而無勸上勤學問者。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wenkui again memorialized, saying: "Since your servant entered the state I have seen many sealed memorials to Your Majesty, yet none urging Your Majesty to study diligently.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wenkui memorialized again: "Since I entered your service I have seen many memorials, yet none urging Your Majesty to pursue learning.

sentences.zh: 上喜閱三國志，此一隅之見，偏而不全。

translations.literal: Your Majesty delights in reading the Records of the Three Kingdoms—this is a view from one corner, partial and not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty enjoys the Records of the Three Kingdoms—a partial view from one corner, not the whole.

sentences.zh: 帝王治平之道，奧在四書，跡詳史籍。

translations.literal: The subtlety of emperors' and kings' way of ordering and pacifying lies in the Four Books; the traces are detailed in historical records.
translations.idiomatic: The art of imperial rule lies in the Four Books; its record is set out in the histories.

sentences.zh: 宜選筆帖式通文義者，秀才老成者，分任移譯講解，日進四書二章，通鑑一章。

translations.literal: You should select clerks who understand literary meaning and mature licentiates, divide the labor of translating and explaining, and daily advance two chapters of the Four Books and one chapter of the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Choose literate clerks and seasoned scholars to translate and lecture in turn, with two chapters of the Four Books and one chapter of the Comprehensive Mirror presented each day.

sentences.zh: 上聽政之暇，日知月積，身體力行，操約而施博，行易而效捷。

translations.literal: In Your Majesty's leisure from hearing government, day by day knowledge accumulates month by month; personally practice it in body, hold the handle simply yet apply it broadly, act easily yet achieve results swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure from governing, let knowledge grow day by day; practice what you learn, hold to simplicity yet act broadly, and achieve results with ease and speed.

sentences.zh: 上無曰'此難能'，更無曰'乃公從馬上得之'，烏用此迂儒之常談，而付之一哂也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not say 'this is hard to accomplish,' still less say 'the old man won it from horseback'—why use these pedantic commonplaces only to dismiss them with a laugh?
translations.idiomatic: Do not say 'that is too hard,' or 'I won the realm on horseback'—do not dismiss such counsel as pedantic talk fit only for a laugh.

sentences.zh: 上用人亦宜詳審，臣第就書房言之。

translations.literal: In employing men Your Majesty should also examine carefully; your servant will speak only of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should also choose men with care; I speak here only of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 書房出納章奏，即南朝之通政司也。

translations.literal: The Secretariat receives and dispatches memorials—it is the Southern Court's Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat handles memorials in and out—it is the counterpart of the Ming Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 自達海卒，龍什罷，五榜式不通漢字，三漢官又無責成。

translations.literal: Since Dahai died and Longshi was dismissed, the five bangshi do not know Chinese characters, and the three Han officials have no fixed responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Since Dahai's death and Longshi's dismissal, the five bangshi cannot read Chinese, and the three Han officials have no clear accountability.

sentences.zh: 秀才八九，閧然而來，群然而散。

translations.literal: Eight or nine licentiates come with a hubbub and disperse in a crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Eight or nine licentiates bustle in together and scatter in a crowd.

sentences.zh: 遇有章奏，彼此相諉，動淹旬月。

translations.literal: When memorials arise they shift blame on one another, often delaying matters for a month or more.
translations.idiomatic: When memorials arrive they pass the blame, and business often stalls for a month or more.

sentences.zh: 上方求言，而令喉舌不通，是何異欲其入而閉之門乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is now seeking counsel, yet you make the throat and tongue unable to speak—how is this different from wanting someone to enter yet closing the door?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty asks for advice yet blocks the channel of speech—how is that unlike inviting someone in and shutting the door?

sentences.zh: 宜量才委用，或分任俾責有所專，或獨任俾事有所總。

translations.literal: You should assign duties according to talent—either divide responsibilities so each charge has its specialist, or entrust one man so affairs have a head.
translations.idiomatic: Assign men by ability—either divide duties so each has a clear charge, or put one man in charge so affairs have a head.

sentences.zh: 至筆帖式通文義者，惟恩國泰一人，宜再擇一二以助不逮。

translations.literal: As for clerks who understand literary meaning, only En Guotai is one; you should choose another one or two to assist where he falls short.
translations.idiomatic: Of clerks who understand literary Chinese, only En Guotai qualifies; choose one or two more to assist him.

sentences.zh: 立簿籍，定期會，使大事不過五，小事不過十，分而任之。

translations.literal: Establish registers, fix regular meetings, let major matters take no more than five days, minor matters no more than ten, divide and assign them.
translations.idiomatic: Keep registers, set regular meetings, allow five days for major business and ten for minor, and divide the work.

sentences.zh: 課勤惰，察能否，而從以賞罰，則政柄不搖，賢愚並勵矣。」

translations.literal: Examine diligence and sloth, observe ability and inability, and follow with rewards and punishments—then the handle of government will not waver and worthy and simple alike will be stirred."
translations.idiomatic: Test diligence and slackness, judge ability, and reward or punish accordingly—then authority will hold firm and all will be stirred to effort."

translations.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: (Wenkui's memorial closed.)

sentences.zh: 七年七月，疏言：「圖事功者，以得人為先務。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year he memorialized, saying: "Those who plan achievement take obtaining men as the first task.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year he wrote: "To achieve great things, finding the right men comes first.

sentences.zh: 頃聞開科取士，誠開創急事也。

translations.literal: I have lately heard of opening the examinations to select scholars—this is indeed an urgent matter for a founding state.
translations.idiomatic: I hear examinations are to be opened to recruit scholars—a pressing need for a new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 然臣以為非掄才之完策，上宜發明諭，不拘族類，不限貴賤，不分新舊，有才能者許自薦，知人有才能者許保舉。

translations.literal: Yet your servant thinks this is not a complete policy for selecting talent; Your Majesty should issue a clear edict, not binding clan or category, not limiting noble and base, not distinguishing new and old—let those with ability be permitted to recommend themselves, and let those who know men of ability be permitted to sponsor them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I do not think examinations alone suffice; issue a clear edict: disregard clan, rank, and whether men are old subjects or new—let the able recommend themselves and let others sponsor talent they know.

sentences.zh: 自薦者擇有智識之臣，畀以掄選，而嚴挾私徇情之罰；

translations.literal: For self-recommendation, choose intelligent ministers, entrust them with selection, and impose strict penalties for favoritism and private feeling;
translations.idiomatic: For self-recommendation, appoint discerning ministers to conduct selection and punish favoritism severely;

sentences.zh: 保舉者不避父子兄弟，但令立狀記籍，異日考其功罪，與同賞罰，然後親加省試，量才錄用。

translations.literal: for sponsorship do not avoid father and son or brothers, but require written pledges recorded in registers; later examine their merit and guilt and share rewards and punishments, then personally add provincial examination and employ according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: for sponsorship do not exclude kin, but require written pledges on record; later judge sponsor and nominee together, then examine candidates yourself and appoint by merit.

sentences.zh: 有技能則超擢，無才行則責譴。

translations.literal: Those with skill are promoted beyond the norm; those without ability or conduct are rebuked and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Promote the skilled beyond ordinary rank; rebuke and punish the incapable.

sentences.zh: 奴隸工商，有善必取。

translations.literal: Among slaves, artisans, and merchants, if there is excellence, take it.
translations.idiomatic: From slaves, artisans, and merchants, take any man of merit.

sentences.zh: 顯官貴戚，有惡必懲。

translations.literal: Among eminent officials and noble kin, if there is evil, punish it.
translations.idiomatic: Among great officials and noble kin, punish every wrong.

sentences.zh: 招以真心實意，歆以高爵厚祿，繩以嚴刑重罰。

translations.literal: Summon with sincere heart and true intent, entice with high ranks and thick stipends, bind with severe punishments and heavy penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Summon men with sincerity, entice them with rank and rich stipends, and restrain them with stern punishment.

sentences.zh: 好榮惡辱，人情所同。

translations.literal: Loving glory and hating disgrace are what human feeling shares alike.
translations.idiomatic: All men alike love honor and hate shame.

sentences.zh: 雖不能拔十得五，於千百中得數人，而已足為用矣。」

translations.literal: Though one cannot pick five from ten, to obtain several men from among thousands and hundreds is already enough for use."
translations.idiomatic: Even if you cannot pick five from ten, a few men out of thousands will suffice."

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，甄別文館諸臣，文奎列第二，賜人戶、牲畜，授內弘文院學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, when the Literary Institute members were ranked, Wenkui was placed second, granted households and livestock, and appointed academician of the Inner Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde (1636), when institute scholars were ranked, Wenkui stood second, received households and livestock, and was made academician of the Inner Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 七年八月，以醉乘馬犯鹵簿，論死，上宥之，仍命斷酒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year, for riding a horse while drunk and violating the imperial escort, he was sentenced to death; the sovereign pardoned him but still ordered him to abstain from wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventh year he was sentenced to death for riding while drunk into the imperial escort; the khan pardoned him but ordered him to give up wine.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，世祖定鼎，七月，命為右副都御史，巡撫保定。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, when the Shizu Emperor fixed the capital, in the seventh month he was ordered to serve as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi (1644), after the Shunzhi Emperor established the capital, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Baoding in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 時畿南未定，保定、大名、真定所屬諸州縣，盜千百並起，焚掠為民害。

translations.literal: At that time the south of the capital district was not yet settled; in the prefectures and counties subordinate to Baoding, Daming, and Zhending, hundreds and thousands of bandits rose together, burning and plundering to the people's harm.
translations.idiomatic: The region south of the capital was still unsettled; in the prefectures under Baoding, Daming, and Zhending, bandits rose by the hundreds and thousands, burning and looting the people.

sentences.zh: 文奎到官，駐真定，訓練所部兵，與巡按衛周胤謀捕治，盜渠趙崇陽等數百人降。

translations.literal: Wenkui reached his post, stationed himself at Zhending, trained the troops under his command, and with investigating censor Wei Zhouyin plotted to capture and punish them; the bandit chieftain Zhao Chongyang and several hundred men surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkui took office at Zhending, drilled his troops, and with censor Wei Zhouyin planned arrests; the bandit leader Zhao Chongyang and several hundred men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 有韓國璧者，為盜寧晉泊，拒官軍。

translations.literal: There was one Han Guobi, who made himself bandit chief at Ningjin Marsh and resisted government troops.
translations.idiomatic: One Han Guobi had made himself bandit chief at Ningjin Marsh and fought the government forces.

sentences.zh: 文奎即用崇陽捕斬國璧，殲其徒。

translations.literal: Wenkui immediately used Chongyang to capture and behead Guobi and annihilate his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkui sent Chongyang to capture and execute Guobi and destroy his band.

sentences.zh: 遂分部總兵王巇、守備劉文選等將兵逐賊。

translations.literal: He then divided his forces, with Regional Commander Wang Xi, Garrison Commander Liu Wenxuan, and others leading troops to pursue the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched Regional Commander Wang Xi, Garrison Commander Liu Wenxuan, and others to hunt down the bandits.

sentences.zh: 巇等討滅香爐、喬家二寨，戮其渠錢子亮、趙建英。

translations.literal: Xi and the others suppressed and destroyed the two stockades at Xianglu and Qiaojia, executing their chieftains Qian Ziliang and Zhao Jianying.
translations.idiomatic: Xi destroyed the stockades at Xianglu and Qiaojia and executed the chiefs Qian Ziliang and Zhao Jianying.

sentences.zh: 文選等攻深州，戮其渠於小安；

translations.literal: Wenxuan and the others attacked Shenzhou and executed its chieftain at Xiao'an;
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan attacked Shenzhou and executed its chief at Xiao'an;

sentences.zh: 攻晉州，戮其渠馬數全。

translations.literal: they attacked Jinzhou and executed its chieftain Ma Shuquan.
translations.idiomatic: then attacked Jinzhou and executed its chief Ma Shuquan.

sentences.zh: 於是冀州郭世先、保定李庫、內黃李君相、順德袁三才數十渠魁，並就俘戮。

translations.literal: Thereupon dozens of chieftains including Guo Shixian of Jizhou, Li Ku of Baoding, Li Junxiang of Neihuang, and Yuan Sancai of Shunde were captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of bandit chiefs—including Guo Shixian of Jizhou, Li Ku of Baoding, Li Junxiang of Neihuang, and Yuan Sancai of Shunde—were captured and killed.

sentences.zh: 散其脅從，錄驍勇置部下。

translations.literal: Their compelled followers were dispersed; the brave were enrolled and placed in his command.
translations.idiomatic: Their followers were dispersed; the brave were enrolled in his forces.

sentences.zh: 畿南漸定。

translations.literal: The south of the capital district gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: The region south of the capital gradually grew calm.

sentences.zh: 州縣吏徵賦仍​​明季舊習，優免多則蝕賦，攤派行則厲民，文奎疏請悉從正額；

translations.literal: Prefectural and county officials still levied taxes according to late-Ming habits—many exemptions then eroded the tax quota, and when assessments were spread out the people were harried; Wenkui memorialized requesting that all follow the regular quota;
translations.idiomatic: Local officials still collected taxes by late-Ming custom, eroding the quota through excessive exemptions or harrying the people through reassessment; Wenkui asked that only the regular levy be taken;

sentences.zh: 寧晉泊地肥而賦輕，豪右競佔，逋賦為州縣吏累，文奎疏請招民分耕納賦；

translations.literal: the land at Ningjin Marsh was fertile yet lightly taxed; powerful families competed to seize it, and arrears became a burden on prefectural and county officials; Wenkui memorialized requesting that commoners be recruited to divide the land for cultivation and pay taxes;
translations.idiomatic: Ningjin Marsh was fertile but lightly taxed; gentry seized it and arrears burdened local officials; Wenkui asked that settlers be recruited to farm it and pay tax;

sentences.zh: 二年正月，疏言畿南民重困，歲貢綿絲諸品，皆求諸他行省，請改折色；

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he memorialized that the people south of the capital were heavily afflicted; annual tribute of silk floss and other goods was all sought from other provinces—he requested conversion to commutation payments;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year he reported that the people south of the capital were in deep distress; annual tribute of silk and other goods was procured from other provinces—he asked that it be commuted to silver;

sentences.zh: 二月，又論諸衛所地納賦丁入保甲，皆當屬州縣吏：並見採擇。

translations.literal: In the second month he again argued that land tax and corvée labor of the guard posts and enrolled households in the baojia system should all fall under prefectural and county officials—all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he argued that guard-post lands, tax quotas, corvée labor, and baojia registration should all fall under county officials—all were approved.

sentences.zh: 李聯芳、張成軒等為盜南皮、鹽山間，四月，遣都司楊澄、守備徐景山捕治，戮聯芳等九十三人。

translations.literal: Li Lianfang, Zhang Chengxuan, and others were bandits between Nanpi and Yanshan; in the fourth month he dispatched Brigade Commander Yang Cheng and Garrison Commander Xu Jingshan to capture and punish them, executing Lianfang and ninety-three others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lianfang and Zhang Chengxuan led bandits between Nanpi and Yanshan; in the fourth month he sent Brigade Commander Yang Cheng and Garrison Commander Xu Jingshan against them and executed Lianfang and ninety-three others.

sentences.zh: 尋命加兵部右侍郎，總督陝西。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and made governor-general of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and appointed governor-general of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 五月，改命總督淮、揚漕運。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was reassigned to govern the Huai-Yang grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was reassigned to oversee Huai-Yang grain transport.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚群盜，高進忠、魏用通、高升三人者為之魁，復有酆報國、司邦基挾明宗室新昌王，與相應為亂。

translations.literal: Bandits swarmed in Huai and Yang; Gao Jinzhong, Wei Yongtong, and Gao Sheng were their chiefs, and moreover Feng Baoguo and Si Bangji took the Ming imperial clansman the Prince of Xinchang and joined in rebellion with them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits plagued Huai and Yang; Gao Jinzhong, Wei Yongtong, and Gao Sheng led them, while Feng Baoguo and Si Bangji backed the Ming clansman Prince of Xinchang in revolt.

sentences.zh: 文奎遣游擊裴應暘等擊斬用通，總兵王天寵亦擊破升，報國、邦基為其徒縛詣江寧以降；

translations.literal: Wenkui dispatched Mobile Corps Commander Pei Yingyang and others to strike and behead Yongtong; Regional Commander Wang Tianchong also defeated Sheng; Baoguo and Bangji were bound by their own followers and sent to Jiangning to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Wenkui sent Mobile Corps Commander Pei Yingyang to kill Yongtong; Regional Commander Wang Tianchong routed Sheng; Baoguo and Bangji were bound by their own men and sent to surrender at Jiangning;

sentences.zh: 進忠走崇明，亦降。

translations.literal: Jinzhong fled to Chongming and also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong fled to Chongming and surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 十二月，復令總兵孔希貴、蘇希樂逐盜如皋，得其渠於錫籓、劉一雄。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he again ordered Regional Commanders Kong Xigui and Su Xile to pursue bandits at Rugao and captured their chieftains Yu Xifan and Liu Yixiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he sent Regional Commanders Kong Xigui and Su Xile to hunt bandits at Rugao and captured the chiefs Yu Xifan and Liu Yixiong.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，又與淮徐道張兆熊發兵擊斬邳州盜楊秉孝、王君實等。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, together with Huai-Xu Circuit Intendant Zhang Zhaoxiong, he again raised troops and struck down the bandits of Pizhou, Yang Bingxiao, Wang Junshi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year, with Circuit Intendant Zhang Zhaoxiong of Huai-Xu, he sent troops against the Pizhou bandits Yang Bingxiao, Wang Junshi, and others and killed them.

sentences.zh: 江、淮間始稍安。

translations.literal: The region between the Yangtze and Huai gradually grew somewhat calm.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze-Huai region gradually grew calmer.

sentences.zh: 十月，疏請禁革蘇、松諸府徵漕積弊，悉去官戶、儒戶、濟農倉諸名，著為令。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he memorialized requesting the prohibition and reform of accumulated abuses in grain transport levies in Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures, entirely abolishing the designations of official households, scholar households, relief granaries, and the like, and establishing them as statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he asked that abuses in grain transport levies in Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures be banned, that labels such as official households, scholar households, and relief granaries be abolished, and that the reforms be codified as law.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，以擅免荒田賦，又瀆請明陵祀典，奪職。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, for arbitrarily exempting tax on wasteland and irreverently petitioning regarding sacrifices at the Ming imperial tombs, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he was dismissed for exempting wasteland tax without authority and for an improper petition about rites at the Ming imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，起為內弘文院學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year he was recalled to serve as academician of the Inner Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year he was recalled as academician of the Inner Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 六年，充會試總裁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as chief examiner of the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 八年，大學士剛林、祁充格得罪，文奎以知睿親王多爾袞令改實錄不上言，當坐，上命免議。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Grand Secretaries Ganglin and Qi Chongge were found guilty; Wenkui, for knowing that Prince Regent Dorgon had ordered alterations to the Veritable Records yet not reporting it, should have been punished, but the sovereign ordered the case waived.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Grand Secretaries Ganglin and Qi Chongge were condemned; Wenkui had known of Prince Regent Dorgon's order to alter the Veritable Records without reporting it and should have been punished, but the emperor excused him.

sentences.zh: 四月，復命以兵部侍郎、左副都御史，總督漕運，巡撫鳳陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was again ordered to serve as Vice Minister of War and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, governor of grain transport, and grand coordinator of Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was again appointed Vice Minister of War and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, with charge of grain transport and the governorship of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 請復姓沈氏。

translations.literal: He requested restoration of the surname Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resume the surname Shen.

sentences.zh: 七月，疏請慎選運官，清核舍餘，合選殷丁，清勾黃快，皆漕政大端，凡四事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he memorialized requesting careful selection of transport officials, thorough audit of surplus grain, proper selection of sturdy laborers, and clearing of yellow-fast runners—all major points of transport administration, four matters in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he memorialized on four major points of transport policy: careful selection of transport officials, audit of surplus grain, recruitment of able laborers, and clearing of courier runners.

sentences.zh: 十年，率師討膠州叛將海時行。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he led troops to attack the Jiaozhou rebel general Hai Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he led an expedition against the Jiaozhou rebel Hai Shixing.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遣兵捕硃週錤，清通、泰濱海逋寇。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he dispatched troops to capture Zhu Zhoujin and clear bandits along the Tong, Tai, and Binhai coasts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he sent troops to capture Zhu Zhoujin and clear coastal bandits in Tongzhou, Taizhou, and Binhai.

sentences.zh: 江北廬、鳳、淮、揚諸府災，文奎請蠲賦，戶部議未定，冬盡未啟徵。

translations.literal: Disaster struck the prefectures of Luzhou, Fengyang, Huai'an, and Yangzhou north of the Yangtze; Wenkui requested tax relief, the Ministry of Revenue had not yet decided, and by winter's end collection had not begun.
translations.idiomatic: When Luzhou, Fengyang, Huai'an, and Yangzhou north of the Yangtze suffered disaster, Wenkui asked for tax relief; the Ministry of Revenue had not yet ruled, and collection had not begun by winter's end.

sentences.zh: 九月，文奎坐督運愆遲，左遷陝西督糧道。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wenkui was punished for delay in supervising transport and demoted to grain transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was demoted to Shaanxi grain transport commissioner for delays in supervising transport.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 與文奎同時以諸生直文館者，雲深、應時同被召對。

translations.literal: Those who, like Wenkui, served in the Literary Institute as licentiates at the same time included Yunshen and Yingshi, who were likewise summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiates who served in the Literary Institute at the same time as Wenkui, including Yunshen and Yingshi, were also summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 又有李棲鳳、楊方興、高士俊、馬國柱、馬鳴佩、雷興輩，蓋皆文奎疏中所謂秀才八九者也。

translations.literal: There were also Li Qifeng, Yang Fangxing, Gao Shijun, Ma Guozhu, Ma Mingpei, Lei Xing, and others—probably the "eight or nine licentiates" of whom Wenkui spoke in his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Li Qifeng, Yang Fangxing, Gao Shijun, Ma Guozhu, Ma Mingpei, Lei Xing, and others—likely the "eight or nine licentiates" Wenkui mentioned in his memorial.

sentences.zh: 棲鳳、方興、國柱、鳴佩、興自有傳。

translations.literal: Qifeng, Fangxing, Guozhu, Mingpei, and Xing have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Qifeng, Fangxing, Guozhu, Mingpei, and Xing have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 雲深後不著。

translations.literal: Yunshen later left no further record.
translations.idiomatic: Yunshen later drops from the record.

sentences.zh: 應時為啟心郎，以祝世昌請毋以俘婦為妓，為改疏稿，坐死。

translations.literal: Yingshi served as qixinlang; at Zhu Shichang's request that captive women not be made courtesans, he altered the memorial draft and was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi served as qixinlang; when Zhu Shichang asked that captive women not be made courtesans, he changed the memorial draft and was executed.

sentences.zh: 士俊嘗上疏謂：「上定例一丁予田五日，衣食於此出，力役於此出。

translations.literal: Shijun once memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty fixed the rule that one adult male receives five days' worth of fields; food and clothing come from this, and corvée labor comes from this.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun once wrote: "Your Majesty decreed that each adult male receive fields equivalent to five days' provision; from this come food, clothing, and labor service.

sentences.zh: 民已苦不足，況以繩量田，名五日，實止二三日。

translations.literal: The people already suffer insufficiency; moreover, when measuring fields by the cord, though called five days, in fact only two or three days remain.
translations.idiomatic: The people already lack enough; when fields are measured by the cord, though called five days' worth, in practice only two or three days remain.

sentences.zh: 將吏复佔沃地，役民以耕，宜禁革。

translations.literal: Officers again seize fertile land and compel the people to farm it—this should be prohibited and reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Officers seize fertile land and force the people to farm it—this should be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 民間貸金，當視金多寡定取息重輕，其有逾度者，宜坐罪。」

translations.literal: When the people lend gold, interest should be set according to how much gold is lent, heavy or light; those who exceed the limit should be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Private loans should bear interest proportionate to the sum; those who charge excessive interest should be punished."

sentences.zh: 日者，滿洲以計田，土俊用當時語也。

translations.literal: Recently the Manchus used jitan to calculate fields—Shijun used the contemporary term.
translations.idiomatic: The Manchus had lately used jitan to survey fields—Shijun used the term current at the time.

sentences.zh: 士俊入關後，嘗為湖廣巡撫，收長沙，克衡州、常德，有勞。

translations.literal: After Shijun entered the Pass he once served as grand coordinator of Huguang, recovered Changsha, and captured Hengzhou and Changde, with merit.
translations.idiomatic: After entering China proper, Shijun served as governor of Huguang, recovered Changsha, and took Hengzhou and Changde with distinction.

sentences.zh: 方上召文奎等策議和成否，亦諭吏民令建言。

translations.literal: Just when the sovereign summoned Wenkui and others to deliberate whether peace could be achieved, he also instructed officials and commoners to offer counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When the khan summoned Wenkui and others to debate peace, he also ordered officials and commoners to submit advice.

sentences.zh: 有胡貢明者，疏言：「我國與南朝未嘗無內外君臣之分。

translations.literal: There was one Hu Gongming, who memorialized, saying: "Our state and the Southern Court have never lacked the distinction of inner and outer, subject and sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Gongming memorialized: "Our state and the Ming have always recognized the distinction between subject and sovereign, inner and outer.

sentences.zh: 今既議和，當遣使修表，姑聽其區畫。

translations.literal: Now that peace is under discussion, envoys should be sent to present memorials in proper form, and for the moment their arrangements should be heard.
translations.idiomatic: If peace is sought, send envoys with formal memorials and for the moment accept their arrangements.

sentences.zh: 如不欲為之下，遂圖大事，必如漢高祖而後可。」

translations.literal: If you do not wish to stand beneath them and instead pursue great affairs, you must be like Emperor Gaozu of Han before it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse subordination and aim at greater things, you must act like Emperor Gaozu of Han."

sentences.zh: 因謂鼓舞用人，養百姓，立法令，收人心，皆未若漢高祖。

translations.literal: He therefore said that in inspiring and employing men, nurturing the common people, establishing laws, and winning hearts, none had yet equaled Gaozu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He held that in rousing men to service, caring for the people, making laws, and winning hearts, none yet matched Gaozu of Han.

sentences.zh: 貢明先嘗上疏請更養人舊例，略言：「太祖時方草創，土地、人民、財用皆與諸貝勒均之。

translations.literal: Gongming had earlier memorialized requesting revision of the old regulations for nurturing the people, briefly saying: "In the Taizu Emperor's time, when the state was first being founded, land, people, and wealth were all shared equally with the beile.
translations.idiomatic: Gongming had earlier asked that old rules for supporting the people be revised, writing: "Under the Taizu Emperor, when the state was being founded, land, people, and wealth were shared equally among the princes.

sentences.zh: 今尚沿此習，上名雖有國，實不啻正黃旗一貝勒耳。

translations.literal: That custom is still followed today; though Your Majesty bears the name of having a state, in fact you are no more than a beile of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: That practice continues; though Your Majesty bears the title of ruler, in effect you are little more than a Plain Yellow Banner prince.

sentences.zh: 一人寸土，上與諸貝勒互不相容。

translations.literal: For every inch of soil, Your Majesty and the beile cannot accommodate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Every inch of land pits Your Majesty against the princes.

sentences.zh: 十羊九牧，即有中原不可以為治。

translations.literal: Ten shepherds for nine sheep—even with the Central Plain, rule cannot be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Ten masters for nine servants—even with the Central Plain, government cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 出師得財，當以三屬上，七分畀諸貝勒。

translations.literal: When campaigns yield wealth, three-tenths should go to Your Majesty and seven-tenths to the beile.
translations.idiomatic: Spoils of war should go three-tenths to Your Majesty and seven-tenths to the princes.

sentences.zh: 得人聚而贖之，視其賢不賢，厚薄予奪，權得以自操，而人心亦歸於一。」

translations.literal: Gather men and ransom them back, judging worthy and unworthy, granting generously or withholding—then authority can be wielded independently and hearts will unite in one."
translations.idiomatic: Ransom captured men back, judge their merit, reward or withhold accordingly—then you hold power yourself and hearts unite."

sentences.zh: 至是又別疏申前說，並反覆言養豪傑當破格，如高祖之於「三傑」。

translations.literal: At this time he again submitted a separate memorial elaborating his earlier argument, and repeatedly said that nurturing heroes requires breaking convention, as Gaozu did with the 'Three Outstanding Men.'"
translations.idiomatic: He now submitted another memorial repeating his argument, insisting that nurturing heroes requires exceptional treatment, as Gaozu treated the Three Outstanding Men."

sentences.zh: 上覽先疏，頗韙其語，謂後出師當用汝議；

translations.literal: The sovereign read his earlier memorial and largely approved his words, saying that on the next campaign his plan should be used;
translations.idiomatic: The khan read his earlier memorial and largely agreed, saying his plan would be used on the next campaign;

sentences.zh: 覽後疏，責其語冗。

translations.literal: reading the later memorial, he rebuked its verbosity.
translations.idiomatic: but found the later memorial wordy and rebuked it.

sentences.zh: 貢明復上疏抗辨。

translations.literal: Gongming again memorialized in rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: Gongming memorialized again in defense.

sentences.zh: 七年，又有扈應元者，疏詆漢官但求名利，語近戇，略如貢明。

translations.literal: In the seventh year there was also Hu Yingyuan, whose memorial slandered Han officials as caring only for fame and profit; his language was nearly blunt, much like Gongming's.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Hu Yingyuan also memorialized, accusing Han officials of seeking only fame and profit in language nearly as blunt as Gongming's.

sentences.zh: 別疏陳七事，謂備荒宜儲糧；

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he set forth seven matters, saying that for famine preparedness grain should be stored;
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he listed seven points: for famine relief, store grain;

sentences.zh: 編丁宜卹老；

translations.literal: for registering adult males, the aged and infirm should be shown compassion;
translations.idiomatic: in registering households, show compassion to the aged and weak;

sentences.zh: 築城建關宜不妨農業；

translations.literal: in building cities and frontier passes, agriculture should not be hindered;
translations.idiomatic: in building cities and passes, do not harm farming;

sentences.zh: 出師宜選公正廉能吏，拊循新下郡邑；

translations.literal: on campaign, upright and incorruptible officials should be chosen to comfort newly submitted prefectures and counties;
translations.idiomatic: on campaign, send upright officials to pacify newly submitted districts;

sentences.zh: 取士宜尚德行；

translations.literal: in selecting scholars, virtue should be prized;
translations.idiomatic: in recruiting scholars, value character;

sentences.zh: 求言宜置諫官；

translations.literal: in seeking counsel, remonstrating officials should be appointed;
translations.idiomatic: in seeking advice, appoint remonstrating officials;

sentences.zh: 乘機取天下，在人心不在火器。

translations.literal: seizing the realm depends on winning hearts, not on firearms.
translations.idiomatic: winning the realm depends on hearts, not on firearms.

sentences.zh: 上覽其疏，至論築城建關，疑勿善也，不竟閱。

translations.literal: The sovereign read his memorial; when he reached the discussion of building cities and frontier passes he suspected it was not sound and did not finish reading.
translations.idiomatic: Reading his memorial, the khan doubted the passage on building cities and passes and did not finish it.

sentences.zh: 應元亦上疏抗辨。

translations.literal: Yingyuan also memorialized in rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan too memorialized in rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 貢明隸鑲紅旗，亦諸生；

translations.literal: Gongming was enrolled in the Bordered Red Banner; he too was a licentiate;
translations.idiomatic: Gongming belonged to the Bordered Red Banner and was a licentiate;

sentences.zh: 應元隸正白旗，自署「隱士」。

translations.literal: Yingyuan belonged to the Plain White Banner and styled himself "Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan belonged to the Plain White Banner and called himself "Recluse."

sentences.zh: 李棲鳳，字瑞梧，廣寧人，本貫陝西武威。

translations.literal: Li Qifeng, style Ruiwu, was a native of Guangning; his original domicile was Wuwei in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qifeng, courtesy name Ruiwu, was from Guangning; his ancestral home was Wuwei in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父維新，仕明為四川總兵官。

translations.literal: His father Weixin served the Ming as regional commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Weixin had been Ming regional commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗官薊、遼，家焉。

translations.literal: He had once held office in Ji and Liaodong and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: He had served in Ji and Liaodong and settled there.

sentences.zh: 馬鳴佩字潤甫，遼陽人，本貫山東蓬萊。

translations.literal: Ma Mingpei, style Runfu, was a native of Liaoyang; his original domicile was Penglai in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Mingpei, courtesy name Runfu, was from Liaoyang; his ancestral home was Penglai in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 其先世嘗為遼東保義副將，因佔籍遼陽左衛。

translations.literal: His ancestors had once served as deputy defender-general of Liaodong and for that reason were registered in the Liaoyang Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had been deputy defender-general of Liaodong and were registered in the Liaoyang Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 棲鳳、鳴佩皆以諸生來歸，事太宗，並值文館。

translations.literal: Qifeng and Mingpei both came over as licentiates, served the Taizong, and were both assigned to the Literary Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Qifeng and Mingpei both submitted as licentiates, served Hong Taiji, and were assigned to the Literary Institute.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，甄別文館諸臣，棲鳳、鳴佩俱列二等，賜人戶、牲畜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, when institute members were ranked, Qifeng and Mingpei were both placed in the second grade and granted households and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde both were ranked second among institute scholars and received households and livestock.

sentences.zh: 漢軍旗制定，同隸鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: When the Han banners were established, both were enrolled in the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han banners were organized, both entered the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎，授棲鳳山東東昌道，鳴佩山西冀南道。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor fixed the capital, Qifeng was appointed to the Dongchang Circuit of Shandong and Mingpei to the Jinan Circuit of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shunzhi Emperor established the capital, Qifeng was made intendant of Dongchang in Shandong and Mingpei of Jinan in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，收湖廣，移棲鳳上荊南道，鳴佩下湖南道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, when Huguang was recovered, Qifeng was moved to the Upper Jingnan Circuit and Mingpei to the Lower Hunan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 2, when Huguang was recovered, Qifeng was transferred to Upper Jingnan and Mingpei to Lower Hunan.

sentences.zh: 方棲鳳值文館，治事勤慎，達海等聞於上。

translations.literal: When Qifeng was serving in the Literary Institute, he handled affairs diligently and cautiously, and Dahai and others reported this to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: While Qifeng served in the Literary Institute he worked diligently, and Dahai reported him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上命司撰擬，移寫國書。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered him to draft documents and transcribe state letters.
translations.idiomatic: The khan ordered him to draft documents and copy state correspondence.

sentences.zh: 達海卒，棲鳳言文館無專責，櫝貯官文書，人得竊視，慮有漏言。

translations.literal: After Dahai died, Qifeng said the Literary Institute had no fixed responsibility; official documents were stored in a chest and anyone could steal a look, which he feared might leak words.
translations.idiomatic: After Dahai's death Qifeng warned that the institute had no clear charge; official papers lay in a chest where anyone might read them and leak secrets.

sentences.zh: 上召王文奎等諮和議成否，棲鳳上疏言：「臣侍文館幾七年，今上與南朝議和，謀及群臣。

translations.literal: When the sovereign summoned Shen Wenkui and others to advise on whether peace could be achieved, Qifeng memorialized, saying: "Your servant has attended the Literary Institute for nearly seven years; now Your Majesty discusses peace with the Southern Court and consults the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the khan summoned Shen Wenkui and others on peace, Qifeng wrote: "I have served the Literary Institute nearly seven years; Your Majesty now consults the ministers on peace with the Ming.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為時政有可惜者二，當速圖者六。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks there are two matters in current policy to be regretted and six that should be urgently planned.
translations.idiomatic: I see two regrettable trends in policy and six matters needing urgent action.

sentences.zh: 先帝勞心力、訓練勁旅以遺上，上當法先帝賞罰出獨斷，有功雖賤雖仇必賞，有罪雖貴雖親必罰。

translations.literal: The late emperor toiled in mind and strength and trained crack troops to bequeath to Your Majesty; Your Majesty should emulate the late emperor in rewards and punishments issued from independent decision—whoever has merit, though base or an enemy, must be rewarded; whoever has guilt, though noble or kin, must be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The late khan trained crack troops for Your Majesty; follow his example in rewards and punishments from your own judgment—reward merit though the man be base or an enemy, punish guilt though he be noble or kin.

sentences.zh: 若不振奮鼓舞，必且習為洩洩，弛已成之業。

translations.literal: If you do not rouse and inspire them, they will surely grow slack and relax the achievements already made.
translations.idiomatic: Without vigorous leadership they will grow slack and undo what has been achieved.

sentences.zh: 此可惜者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first matter to be regretted.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first regret.

sentences.zh: 上天姿英敏，誠大有為之君也。

translations.literal: Heaven has endowed Your Majesty with keen intelligence; you are truly a ruler capable of great deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has given Your Majesty keen intelligence; you are truly a ruler of great promise.

sentences.zh: 臣見諸臣章奏，輒曰'上寬仁大度'，此則諛耳。

translations.literal: I see in the ministers' memorials they always say 'Your Majesty is magnanimous and broad-minded'—this is flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers always call Your Majesty magnanimous—that is flattery.

sentences.zh: 創國之君，不欲過刻，亦不欲過寬。

translations.literal: A founder of a state should not wish to be too harsh, nor should he wish to be too lenient.
translations.idiomatic: A founding ruler should be neither too harsh nor too lenient.

sentences.zh: 用人聽言，審察其可否，中夜而思，如何使人畏，如何使人喜，而後可以驅使。

translations.literal: In employing men and hearing words, examine what is feasible; think in the middle of the night how to make men fear and how to make men rejoice, and only then can you drive them.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing men and hearing counsel, test what will work; ponder by night how to inspire fear and joy, and only then can you command men.

sentences.zh: 倘信虛譽而毗於仁厚，必誤上英敏矣。

translations.literal: If you trust empty praise and side with indulgent kindness, you will surely mislead Your Majesty's keen intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Trust empty praise and lean toward indulgence, and you will waste Your Majesty's keen gifts.

sentences.zh: 此可惜者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second matter to be regretted.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second regret.

sentences.zh: 民以食為天。

translations.literal: The people take food as Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The people live by grain.

sentences.zh: 今歲水且螟，米值驟昂。

translations.literal: This year there is flood and locusts, and the price of rice has suddenly soared.
translations.idiomatic: Floods and locusts have sent rice prices soaring.

sentences.zh: 上宜速出師攻關外八城，八城為我有，豈復慮我民之枵腹耶？

translations.literal: Your Majesty should swiftly send troops to attack the eight cities beyond the passes; once the eight cities are ours, need we still fear our people going hungry?
translations.idiomatic: Strike swiftly at the eight garrison towns beyond the passes; once they are ours, our people will not go hungry.

sentences.zh: 一失此機，民無食且流散，國亦稍稍衰矣。

translations.literal: Miss this opportunity and the people will lack food and scatter; the state too will gradually decline.
translations.idiomatic: Miss this chance and the people will starve and flee, and the state will weaken.

sentences.zh: 當速圖者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first matter to be urgently planned.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first urgent matter.

sentences.zh: 上舊得人民，兵農工役，物物皆備。

translations.literal: Your Majesty formerly gained people in whom soldiers, farmers, artisans, and laborers were all complete in every category.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once held a full complement of soldiers, farmers, artisans, and laborers.

sentences.zh: 惟頻歲役民築城，此毀彼建，不得休，民未必無怨。

translations.literal: Only in successive years the people have been levied to build walls—destroying here and building there, without rest—and the people cannot be without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet year after year the people are levied for wall-building, torn down here and raised there without rest—they cannot help resenting it.

sentences.zh: 昨聞大凌河西夷復加誅戮，奈何先與之誓而後又殺之也？

translations.literal: I have lately heard that tribesmen west of Dalinghe were again put to the sword—why first swear to them and then kill them?
translations.idiomatic: I hear tribesmen west of Dalinghe were slaughtered again—why swear peace and then kill them?

sentences.zh: 今宜罷非時之工，廣養人之惠。

translations.literal: Now you should halt untimely labor and extend the grace of nurturing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Halt untimely projects and extend kindness to the people.

sentences.zh: 當速圖者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second matter to be urgently planned.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second urgent matter.

sentences.zh: 南朝東西支梧，奔命不遑，勢必且南遷。

translations.literal: The Southern Court is strained east and west, unable to attend to all demands, and will surely move south.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming is torn between east and west and must soon move the capital south.

sentences.zh: 祖大壽與上嘗有盟約，當急遣使遊說，乘機進兵，遲則失時。

translations.literal: Zu Dashou once made a covenant with Your Majesty; envoys should be sent at once to persuade him, and troops advanced while the moment lasts—delay and the time is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Dashou once pledged with Your Majesty; send envoys to win him and advance while you can—delay and the moment passes.

sentences.zh: 當速圖者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third matter to be urgently planned.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third urgent matter.

sentences.zh: 君雖聖，必賴賢臣以調燮之。

translations.literal: Though the ruler is sage, he must rely on worthy ministers to harmonize affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even a sage ruler needs worthy ministers to govern.

sentences.zh: 近雖有二三骨鯁之臣，位卑祿薄，信任未專。

translations.literal: Lately there are only two or three blunt-speaking ministers, low in rank and stipend, not yet fully trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Only two or three blunt ministers remain, low in rank and stipend and not fully trusted.

sentences.zh: 如永平道張春，在彼中號有謀略，上宜隆以禮遇，心雖金石，將為我鎔。

translations.literal: Zhang Chun of Yongping Circuit is called resourceful among them; Your Majesty should honor him with ceremony—though his heart were metal or stone, it would melt for us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun of Yongping is counted resourceful among them; honor him generously—even a heart of stone would melt for us.

sentences.zh: 我國雖邊鄙，未始無才，重賞之下，必有勇夫。

translations.literal: Though our state is a frontier land, talent is not lacking; under heavy rewards brave men will surely come forth.
translations.idiomatic: Our frontier state has talent; generous rewards will bring forth brave men.

sentences.zh: 當速圖者四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth matter to be urgently planned.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth urgent matter.

sentences.zh: 諸臣多請制定衣冠，尚未允行。

translations.literal: Many ministers have asked to fix dress and caps, but this has not yet been approved.
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers have asked for dress regulations, but none have been approved.

sentences.zh: 夫所謂衣冠，豈必如南朝紗帽圓領而後可？

translations.literal: What are called dress and caps—must they be like the Southern Court's gauze caps and round collars before they can serve?
translations.idiomatic: Must dress mean Southern-style gauze caps and round collars?

sentences.zh: 但能別尊卑，差貴賤，即是制度。

translations.literal: So long as noble and base can be distinguished and high and low differed, that is regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Distinguishing noble from base is regulation enough.

sentences.zh: 國體威嚴視斯，人心系戀視斯，綱紀法度，風移俗易，莫不視斯。

translations.literal: The dignity of the state depends on this; the people's attachment depends on this; codes, discipline, law, custom, and change of manners all depend on this.
translations.idiomatic: State dignity, popular loyalty, law, and custom all depend on it.

sentences.zh: 當速圖者五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth matter to be urgently planned.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth urgent matter.

sentences.zh: 達海竭心力奉上，及其卒，斂乃無鞾，其廉若此，未聞上破格矜卹。

translations.literal: Dahai exhausted mind and strength in serving Your Majesty; when he died, his effects contained not even boots—so incorrupt was he—yet I have not heard Your Majesty break convention to show compassionate relief.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai gave his all to Your Majesty; at his death he left not even boots—so honest was he—yet I hear no exceptional mark of favor for his family.

sentences.zh: 總兵布三取遼陽首功，先帝賜敕免死，今以事奪官，且下之獄，不過以愚直得罪。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Bu San took first merit at the capture of Liaoyang; the late emperor granted an edict exempting him from death, yet now for an affair his office is stripped and he is cast into prison—nothing more than offense through blunt honesty.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Bu San won first merit at Liaoyang and received an imperial edict sparing his life; now he is stripped of office and imprisoned for nothing more than blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 功過貪廉，自古無全才，不可拘於一。

translations.literal: Merit and fault, greed and integrity—from antiquity no man has been wholly accomplished; one cannot be bound by a single flaw.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity no man combined every virtue; one fault should not undo a man.

sentences.zh: 當速圖者六也。」

translations.literal: This is the sixth matter to be urgently planned."
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth urgent matter."

sentences.zh: 調為上荊南道參政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as vice commissioner of the Upper Jingnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of Upper Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，遷湖廣右布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year he was promoted to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the sixth month, he was promoted to Right Provincial Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十月，命以右副都御史巡撫安徽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was ordered to serve as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 吳繼、程國柱等為寇休寧、婺源間，棲鳳檄總兵李仲興、許漢鼎等帥師捕治，獲所置總兵江烏、鄭恩祥，降張天麒、江周等千人。

translations.literal: Wu Ji, Cheng Guozhu, and others were bandits between Xiuning and Wuyuan; Qifeng dispatched Regional Commanders Li Zhongxing, Xu Handing, and others to lead troops in capture and punishment, taking the bandit-appointed regional commanders Jiang Wu and Zheng Enxiang and receiving the surrender of Zhang Tianlin, Jiang Zhou, and a thousand others.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ji and Cheng Guozhu raided Xiuning and Wuyuan; Qifeng sent Regional Commanders Li Zhongxing and Xu Handing against them, capturing the rebel generals Jiang Wu and Zheng Enxiang and accepting the surrender of Zhang Tianlin, Jiang Zhou, and a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 其黨趙正挾明瑞昌王誼貴攻宿松，棲鳳率總兵卜從善、冷允登御之洿池，斬千級，獲誼貴及正子捷應，弟允升。

translations.literal: Their associate Zhao Zheng, taking the Ming Prince of Ruichang Yiguigui, attacked Susong; Qifeng led Regional Commanders Bu Congshan and Leng Yundeng to meet them at Wuchi, beheading a thousand men and capturing Yiguigui, Zheng's son Jieying, and younger brother Yunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zheng, backing the Ming Prince of Ruichang, attacked Susong; Qifeng met him at Wuchi with Regional Commanders Bu Congshan and Leng Yundeng, killed a thousand men, and captured the prince, Zheng's son Jieying, and brother Yunsheng.

sentences.zh: 招撫江南大學士洪承疇上其事。

translations.literal: He reported the affair to Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, who had surrendered in the south.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the victory to the surrendered southern grand secretary Hong Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 旋坐屬縣濫徵賦不舉劾，左遷。

translations.literal: Soon he was demoted for not impeaching subordinate counties that levied taxes excessively.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted for failing to impeach counties that levied excessive taxes.

sentences.zh: 六年，復自浙江嘉湖道參議授右僉都御史，巡撫廣西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again appointed from vice commissioner of the Jiahu Circuit in Zhejiang as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled from Jiahu in Zhejiang as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明桂王由榔遣兵略廣東諸郡縣，尚可喜、耿繼茂軍駐廣州，棲鳳駐南雄，為具儲糈。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui Zhu Youlang sent troops to seize prefectures and counties in Guangdong; Shang Kexi and Geng Jimao's armies were stationed at Guangzhou while Qifeng was at Nanxiong, providing stores of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui sent troops into Guangdong; while Shang Kexi and Geng Jimao held Guangzhou, Qifeng at Nanxiong supplied grain.

sentences.zh: 七年，合兵克韶州，並破雷州、廉州諸寨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the combined armies captured Shaozhou and also broke the stockades at Leizhou and Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the allied forces took Shaozhou and broke the stockades at Leizhou and Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，明將曾志建侵韶州，棲鳳令南韶道林嗣琛、游擊張瑋等擊之，斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Ming general Zeng Zhijian invaded Shaozhou; Qifeng ordered the Nanshao Circuit intendant Lin Sichen, Mobile Corps Commander Zhang Wei, and others to attack him, beheading more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Ming general Zeng Zhijian attacked Shaozhou; Qifeng sent Lin Sichen and Zhang Wei against him and killed more than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 九年，遣副將先啟玉等攻欽州，獲叛將李成棟子元胤。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he dispatched Deputy General Xian Qiyu and others to attack Qinzhou and captured the rebel general Li Chengdong's son Yuan Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he sent Deputy General Xian Qiyu against Qinzhou and captured the rebel Li Chengdong's son Yuan Yin.

sentences.zh: 十年，明將李定國自梧州侵肇慶，棲鳳遣兵敗之龍頂岡；

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Ming general Li Dingguo invaded Zhaoqing from Wuzhou; Qifeng sent troops to defeat him at Longding Ridge;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Ming general Li Dingguo invaded Zhaoqing from Wuzhou; Qifeng's troops defeated him at Longding Ridge;

sentences.zh: 尋分遣總兵徐成功、吳進功等復羅定州東安縣。

translations.literal: soon he separately dispatched Regional Commanders Xu Chenggong, Wu Jingong, and others to recover Dong'an County in Luoding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: then sent Regional Commanders Xu Chenggong and Wu Jingong to recover Dong'an in Luoding.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上手書「知方略」三字以賜。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, the sovereign personally wrote the three characters "knows strategy" as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: On report of victory the emperor wrote him three characters: "knows strategy."

sentences.zh: 又遣副將陳武、李之珍徇高州，至沙江。

translations.literal: He again dispatched Deputy Generals Chen Wu and Li Zhizhen to advance on Gaozhou as far as Shajiang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Deputy Generals Chen Wu and Li Zhizhen toward Gaozhou as far as Shajiang.

sentences.zh: 敵循江岸列寨，師渡江縱擊，獲所置副將姚奇、中軍餘元璣等。

translations.literal: The enemy lined stockades along the riverbank; the army crossed the river and struck freely, capturing their appointed deputy general Yao Qi, headquarters officer Yu Yuanji, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy lined the river with stockades; his troops crossed, attacked, and captured deputy general Yao Qi and headquarters officer Yu Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 克化州、吳川縣，焚其壘，殲敵。

translations.literal: They captured Huazhou and Wuchuan County, burned their fortresses, and annihilated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They took Huazhou and Wuchuan, burned the enemy camps, and destroyed their force.

sentences.zh: 以功進兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，考滿，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, when his term review was complete, he was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifteenth year, at term review, he was made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 六月，命總督兩廣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was ordered governor-general of the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was appointed governor-general of the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 時明桂王走雲南，其將陳奇策及明江夏王蘊鑰、德陽王儼錦等據上思州，旁掠諸縣，棲鳳令總兵栗養誌等討之，獲奇策等；

translations.literal: At that time the Ming Prince of Gui had fled to Yunnan; his generals Chen Qice and the Ming Princes of Jiangxia Yunqian and Deyang Yanjin and others held Shangsi Prefecture and raided neighboring counties; Qifeng ordered Regional Commander Su Yangzhi and others to attack them and captured Qice and the others;
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui had fled to Yunnan; his generals Chen Qice and Princes of Jiangxia and Deyang held Shangsi and raided the counties; Qifeng sent Regional Commander Su Yangzhi against them and captured Qice;

sentences.zh: 又剿撫那錦、板強諸寨，定太平、思恩諸府。

translations.literal: he also pacified the stockades at Najin and Banqiang and settled Taiping and Si'en prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: he also pacified the Najin and Banqiang stockades and settled Taiping and Si'en.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十八年九月，分設廣東、廣西兩總督，棲鳳督廣東。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighteenth year Guangdong and Guangxi were separately given governor-generals; Qifeng governed Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighteenth year separate governor-generals were set for Guangdong and Guangxi; Qifeng governed Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以老乞休。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on grounds of age, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年正月，卒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of Kangxi year 3.

sentences.zh: 鳴佩，天聰三年，授工部啟心郎，仍直文館。

translations.literal: Mingpei, in the third year of Tiancong, was appointed qixinlang in the Ministry of Works while still serving in the Literary Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong year 3 Mingpei was made qixinlang in the Ministry of Works while continuing in the Literary Institute.

sentences.zh: 六年，與同官羅綉錦疏論輸糧令，語詳繡錦傳。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he and his colleague Luo Xiujin memorialized on the grain transport regulations; the details are in Xiujin's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he and Luo Xiujin memorialized on grain transport regulations, as recorded in Xiujin's biography.

sentences.zh: 崇德八年，授半個前程。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongde he was granted half a senior clerk's salary.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde year 8 he received half a senior clerk's stipend.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，自下湖南道參政授戶部侍郎銜，總督江南糧儲兼理錢法。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, promoted from vice commissioner of the Lower Hunan Circuit, he was given the rank of Vice Minister of Revenue and made governor of Jiangnan grain stores, also overseeing coinage.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 3, promoted from Lower Hunan, he was given Vice Minister of Revenue rank and made governor of Jiangnan grain stores with charge of coinage.

sentences.zh: 疏言錢法首禁私鑄，犯必誅，並請設錢法道專其責；

translations.literal: He memorialized that coinage policy should above all forbid private casting, with offenders punished by death, and requested a dedicated coinage commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: He urged that private coining be forbidden on pain of death and that a coinage commissioner be appointed;

sentences.zh: 江南軍餉不足，請留關稅佐之：皆議行。

translations.literal: Jiangnan military pay was insufficient and he asked that customs revenue be retained to assist—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: military pay in Jiangnan was short and he asked to retain customs revenue to cover it—all approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，入為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十年，改總督倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to governor of the granary yards as vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became granary governor as vice minister.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，命以兵部左侍郎兼右副都御史，總督宣、大、山西，勸墾宣府、大同荒地三千餘頃。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year he was ordered to serve as Left Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, governor-general of Xuan, Da, and Shanxi, encouraging reclamation of more than three thousand qing of wasteland in Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, second month, he was made Left Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, governor-general of Xuan-Datong and Shanxi, and encouraged reclamation of three thousand-plus qing in Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 盜發平陽，鳴佩令副將許占魁等捕治，分兵扼隘，誅其渠張五等二百八十餘人，降其黨九十餘。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Pingyang; Mingpei ordered Deputy General Xu Zhankui and others to capture and punish them, dividing troops to hold the passes and executing the chieftain Zhang Wu and more than two hundred eighty others, while more than ninety of their followers surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Pingyang he sent Deputy General Xu Zhankui to hold the passes, execute chief Zhang Wu and more than 280 men, and accept the surrender of 90 followers.

sentences.zh: 十月，加兵部尚書，移督江南、江西。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted to Minister of War and transferred to govern Jiangnan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to Minister of War and transferred to Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功為寇海上，陳其綸、汪龍等為明將，號為侯、伯，據郡縣，遙應成功。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Chenggong raided the sea; Chen Qilun, Wang Long, and others were Ming generals styled marquises and earls, holding prefectures and counties and responding to Chenggong from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong raided the coast; Ming generals Chen Qilun and Wang Long, styled marquises and earls, held counties and answered Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 鳴佩檄總兵胡有升等攻其綸瑞金，破大柏山寨。

translations.literal: Mingpei dispatched Regional Commander Hu Yousheng and others to attack Qilun at Ruijin and break the stockade at Dabai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Mingpei sent Regional Commander Hu Yousheng against Qilun at Ruijin and broke the Dabai Mountain stockade.

sentences.zh: 其綸走寧都天心寨，寨民獲以獻；

translations.literal: Qilun fled to Tianxin Stockade in Ningdu; the stockade people captured and presented him;
translations.idiomatic: Qilun fled to Tianxin Stockade in Ningdu, where the inhabitants seized and handed him over;

sentences.zh: 复獲龍九江，並擊破成功之徒胡寧等。

translations.literal: Wang Long was again captured at Jiujiang, and the followers of Chenggong such as Hu Ning were also defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Long was captured at Jiujiang and Chenggong's follower Hu Ning was defeated.
