sentences.zh: 未幾，明將張名振以舟師侵崇明，鳴佩亦以舟師御之，名振敗走，得其副將林正禮等；

translations.literal: Before long the Ming general Zhang Mingzhen invaded Chongming with a fleet; Mingpei also met him with a fleet; Mingzhen was defeated and fled, and his deputy general Lin Zhengli was captured;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ming general Zhang Mingzhen attacked Chongming by sea; Mingpei met him with ships, defeated him, and captured deputy general Lin Zhengli;

sentences.zh: 復周歷松江、崇明諸郡邑，視形勢，疏陳水陸攻守之策。

translations.literal: he again toured Songjiang, Chongming, and other prefectures and counties, surveyed the terrain, and memorialized strategies for attack and defense by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: he then toured Songjiang and Chongming, surveyed the terrain, and memorialized on land and sea defense.

sentences.zh: 會給事中張玉治言江寧提督當移駐蘇州，吳淞宜增兵，上令鳴佩覈議。

translations.literal: When Censor Zhang Yuzhi said the Jiangning commander should move to Suzhou and troops should be added at Wusong, the sovereign ordered Mingpei to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Zhang Yuzhi proposed moving the Jiangning commander to Suzhou and reinforcing Wusong, the emperor ordered Mingpei to review the plan.

sentences.zh: 鳴佩請令江寧提督分兵守劉河、福山，蘇松提督駐吳淞，不煩更增兵，但令與江寧提督互策守禦為犄角。

translations.literal: Mingpei requested that the Jiangning commander divide troops to guard Liuhe and Fushan, that the Suzhou-Songjiang commander be stationed at Wusong without adding troops, but that he and the Jiangning commander coordinate defense as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Mingpei proposed that the Jiangning commander garrison Liuhe and Fushan, the Suzhou-Songjiang commander remain at Wusong without extra troops, and the two coordinate as pincers.

sentences.zh: 得旨，如所議。

translations.literal: An edict approved as he proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 十二月，名振兵复侵崇明，以舟師斷海港，官軍莫能渡，鳴佩密令民束草削★H9，佐軍焚敵舟，俘馘無算，名振夜引去。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Mingzhen's troops again invaded Chongming, using ships to block the sea route so government troops could not cross; Mingpei secretly ordered the people to bundle grass into torches to help the army burn enemy ships, capturing and killing beyond count; Mingzhen withdrew by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Mingzhen again blocked Chongming by sea; Mingpei had civilians bundle straw torches to burn enemy ships, inflicting heavy losses, and Mingzhen withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，降所置總兵顧忠，副將黃忠、董禮等百餘人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year the bandit-appointed regional commander Gu Zhong and deputy generals Huang Zhong, Dong Li, and more than a hundred others surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, first month, rebel general Gu Zhong and deputy generals Huang Zhong, Dong Li, and more than a hundred others surrendered.

sentences.zh: 顧忠故劇盜，號「綱倉顧三」，善水戰，至是降，敵益沮。

translations.literal: Gu Zhong had been a fierce bandit styled "Gangcang Gu the Third," skilled in naval warfare; with his surrender the enemy grew more discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong, a fierce pirate known as "Gangcang Gu the Third," excelled at naval fighting; his surrender further discouraged the enemy.

sentences.zh: 复率參將吳守祖等出海，至浙江獨山破敵。

translations.literal: He again led Regiment Commander Wu Shouzu and others to sea, reaching Dushan in Zhejiang and defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He again put to sea with Regiment Commander Wu Shouzu, reached Dushan in Zhejiang, and defeated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 分兵討吉安、贛州盜，敗之上坪；

translations.literal: Dividing troops he suppressed bandits in Ji'an and Ganzhou, defeating them at Shangping;
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments against bandits in Ji'an and Ganzhou and defeated them at Shangping;

sentences.zh: 討徽州盜，剿花橋諸寨。

translations.literal: he attacked Huizhou bandits and pacified the stockades at Huaqiao.
translations.idiomatic: and against Huizhou bandits he cleared the Huaqiao stockades.

sentences.zh: 閏五月，以目疾乞罷，進三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month, on grounds of eye disease, he requested dismissal and was advanced to the third rank of adaha fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month he retired for eye disease and was advanced to third-rank adaha fan.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年正月，卒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of Kangxi year 5.

sentences.zh: 鳴佩嘗薦梁化鳳有大將才，及成功入攻江寧，賴化鳳破敵。

translations.literal: Mingpei had once recommended Liang Huafeng as possessing great general's talent; when Chenggong attacked Jiangning, it was thanks to Liang Huafeng that the enemy was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Mingpei had recommended Liang Huafeng as a great general; when Chenggong attacked Jiangning, Liang Huafeng broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 棲鳳、鳴佩子弟皆才。

translations.literal: The sons and younger brothers of Qifeng and Mingpei were all talented.
translations.idiomatic: The sons and brothers of Qifeng and Mingpei were all capable men.

sentences.zh: 棲鳳弟棲凰漕運總督加太子太保，棲鶤、棲鸞總兵，棲鳴廣東提督；

translations.literal: Qifeng's younger brother Qihuang was grain transport governor-general with the added title Junior Grand Guardian; Qiyu and Qiluan were regional commanders; Qiming was Guangdong provincial commander;
translations.idiomatic: Qifeng's brother Qihuang was grain transport governor-general and Junior Grand Guardian; Qiyu and Qiluan were regional commanders; Qiming was Guangdong provincial commander;

sentences.zh: 子鎮鼎，亦官廣東提督，加太子太保。

translations.literal: his son Zhending also served as Guangdong provincial commander with the added title Junior Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: his son Zhending also became Guangdong provincial commander and Junior Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 鳴佩子雄鎮，自有傳。

translations.literal: Mingpei's son Xiongzhen has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Mingpei's son Xiongzhen has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 馬國柱，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Ma Guozhu was a native of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guozhu was from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 天聰間，以諸生直文館。

translations.literal: During the Tiancong period he served in the Literary Institute as a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancong era he served in the Literary Institute as a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 六年，諸生胡貢明請更養人舊例，語附見沈文奎傳。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the licentiate Hu Gongming requested revision of the old regulations for nurturing the people; the account is appended in Shen Wenkui's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year licentiate Hu Gongming asked to revise old rules for supporting the people, as noted in Shen Wenkui's biography.

sentences.zh: 國柱上疏，謂：「以家喻國，上猶祖父，諸貝勒猶子弟，而人則妻孥也。

translations.literal: Guozhu memorialized, saying: "Taking the family as analogy to the state, Your Majesty is like the grandfather, the beile like sons and younger brothers, and the people like wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu wrote: "If the state is a family, Your Majesty is the grandfather, the princes are sons and brothers, and the people are wives and children.

sentences.zh: 祖父重持家，子弟喜便嬖，好惡不同，不能迫而從也。

translations.literal: The grandfather stresses household management, the sons and younger brothers delight in favorites; likes and dislikes differ and cannot be forced to agree.
translations.idiomatic: The grandfather must keep house, but sons and brothers love favorites; their tastes differ and cannot be forced into line.

sentences.zh: 我國正直者多貧賤，貪佞者多富貴。

translations.literal: In our state the upright are mostly poor and base, while the greedy and fawning are mostly rich and noble.
translations.idiomatic: In our state upright men are poor while flatterers grow rich.

sentences.zh: 正詘而邪申，欲國之興得乎？

translations.literal: The straight is repressed and the crooked exalted—can the state rise thus?
translations.idiomatic: When honesty is crushed and crookedness exalted, can the state prosper?

sentences.zh: 宜採貢明議，無分新舊人，悉養於上。

translations.literal: You should adopt Gongming's proposal and nurture all alike, old subjects and new, under Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Adopt Gongming's plan and support all people, old and new, under Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 如疑八家分人而贍為先帝舊例，試思先帝時雖曰分贍，而厚薄予奪操之一人。

translations.literal: If you doubt that the eight houses' division of men for support was the late emperor's old rule, consider that even then, though it was called divided support, who granted generously or withheld lay in one man's hand.
translations.idiomatic: If you think the eight houses' shared support was the late khan's rule, remember that even then one man decided who received much or little.

sentences.zh: 今昔相較，果何如乎？

translations.literal: Compare past and present—how do they truly stand?
translations.idiomatic: Compare then and now—what has changed?

sentences.zh: 況善繼志者謂之大孝。

translations.literal: Moreover, he who well continues another's purpose is called greatly filial.
translations.idiomatic: True filial piety is to improve on the founder's work.

sentences.zh: 先帝至今日，亦當更舊習。

translations.literal: From the late emperor to today, old habits should also be changed.
translations.idiomatic: From the late khan to now, old habits should change.

sentences.zh: 苟益於國，何有於小嫌？

translations.literal: If it benefits the state, what matter small resentments?
translations.idiomatic: If it serves the state, why cling to small grievances?

sentences.zh: 且利於八家，而上獨擅焉，誠不可也；

translations.literal: Moreover, it is truly impossible for Your Majesty alone to monopolize what profits the eight houses;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty cannot monopolize what profits the eight houses alone;

sentences.zh: 今養人乃勞事，雖專之，庸何傷？」

translations.literal: nurturing the people is hard labor—even if you monopolize it, what harm?"
translations.idiomatic: supporting the people is hard work—even if you keep that charge yourself, what harm is done?"

translations.literal: (Guozhu's memorial closed.)
translations.idiomatic: (Guozhu's memorial closed.)

sentences.zh: 先是，國柱與高鴻中、鮑承先、寧完我、範文程等合疏請置言官，是疏併申言之；

translations.literal: Earlier Guozhu had joined Gao Hongzhong, Bao Chengxian, Ning Wanwo, Fan Wencheng, and others in a joint memorial requesting remonstrating officials; this memorial repeated the argument;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guozhu had joined Gao Hongzhong, Bao Chenxian, Ning Wanwo, Fan Wencheng, and others in asking for remonstrating officials; this memorial repeated that plea;

sentences.zh: 而諸上書言時事者，扈應元、徐明遠、許世昌、仇震疏中往往及是。

translations.literal: and among those who memorialized on current affairs, Hu Yingyuan, Xu Mingyuan, Xu Shichang, and Qiu Zhen often touched on the same points in their memorials.
translations.idiomatic: and memorialists on current affairs—Hu Yingyuan, Xu Mingyuan, Xu Shichang, and Qiu Zhen—often said the same in their petitions.

sentences.zh: 應元事見沈文奎傳。

translations.literal: Yingyuan's account appears in Shen Wenkui's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan is treated in Shen Wenkui's biography.

sentences.zh: 明遠，明兵部吏，自永平降，隸鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: Mingyuan was a clerk in the Ming Ministry of War; he surrendered from Yongping and was enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan had been a Ming Ministry of War clerk; he surrendered at Yongping and entered the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 疏並請禁交結，定法度，立管屯將吏考課黜陟之制，禁管台將吏掊克士卒，禁八門監榷不得用重秤，豁流亡戶籍，錄閒冗吏，革鬻良人為妓。

translations.literal: His memorial also requested prohibition of factional collusion, fixing of laws, establishing assessment and promotion or dismissal for garrison and farming officers, forbidding garrison officers from extorting soldiers, forbidding the eight gates' tax supervisors from using heavy scales, restoring household registers to fugitives, recording redundant clerks, and abolishing the sale of good people as courtesans.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to ban faction, fix laws, assess garrison and farming officers, stop extortion of soldiers, forbid heavy scales at the eight gates, restore fugitives to the registers, record redundant clerks, and end the sale of decent people as courtesans.

sentences.zh: 世昌，正紅旗牛錄章京。

translations.literal: Shichang was a niru zhangjing of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang was a niru captain of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 疏並請定先帝諡號，建中書府。

translations.literal: His memorial also requested fixing the late emperor's posthumous title and establishing a Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for the late khan's posthumous title and a central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 震，明武進士、都督僉事。

translations.literal: Zhen was a Ming military jinshi and Vice Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had been a Ming military jinshi and Vice Commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 疏自署「俘臣」，並請譯書史，申法律，簡賢才，與明通和。

translations.literal: He styled himself "captive minister" in his memorial and also requested translation of books and histories, clarification of laws, selection of worthy talent, and peace with the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He signed his memorial "captive minister" and asked for translation of histories, clearer laws, selection of talent, and peace with the Ming.

sentences.zh: 八年，太宗命禮部設科取士，中式為舉人，國柱與焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Taizong ordered the Ministry of Rites to hold examinations; Guozhu passed as a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Hong Taiji ordered civil examinations; Guozhu passed as a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 直文館如故。

translations.literal: He continued to serve in the Literary Institute as before.
translations.idiomatic: He continued in the Literary Institute.

sentences.zh: 崇德初，始置都察院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongde the Censorate was first established.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chongde the Censorate was established.

sentences.zh: 三年，授國柱理事官。

translations.literal: In the third year Guozhu was appointed supervising official.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Guozhu was made a supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 漢軍旗制定，隸正白旗。

translations.literal: When the Han banners were established he was enrolled in the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han banners were organized he entered the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關，授左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry into the Pass and was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he entered China with the armies and was made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 師已定大同、代州，七月，命國柱以右副都御史巡撫山西，道昌平，出居庸關，至代州任事。

translations.literal: After the army had settled Datong and Daizhou, in the seventh month Guozhu was ordered to serve as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi; he went by way of Changping, out through Juyong Pass, and reached Daizhou to take up affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Datong and Daizhou were taken, in the seventh month he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Shanxi; he went through Changping and Juyong Pass to Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 師自忻州克太原，國柱進駐太原。

translations.literal: When the army took Taiyuan from Xinzhou, Guozhu advanced and was stationed at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the army took Taiyuan from Xinzhou, Guozhu moved his headquarters to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 師行，任策應。

translations.literal: As the army marched he was responsible for planning support.
translations.idiomatic: As the army advanced he coordinated support.

sentences.zh: 汾州、平陽、潞安、澤州諸府以次底定。

translations.literal: The prefectures of Fenzhou, Pingyang, Lu'an, and Zezhou were settled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fenzhou, Pingyang, Lu'an, and Zezhou were secured in turn.

sentences.zh: 李自成將李過、高一功走保綏德，國柱疏請分兵東西夾擊，使賊首尾不相應，上韙其議。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng's generals Li Guo and Gao Yigong fled to hold Suide; Guozhu memorialized requesting divided forces to strike from east and west so the bandits could not respond at head and tail; the sovereign approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's generals Li Guo and Gao Yigong held Suide; Guozhu asked for a pincer attack from east and west so the rebels could not coordinate; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣游擊楊捷擊斬陽曲盜閻汝龍，別將討嵐縣盜高九英，降四十餘寨。

translations.literal: In the second year he dispatched Mobile Corps Commander Yang Jie to strike and behead the Yangqu bandit Yan Rulong; another commander suppressed the Lanxian bandit Gao Jiuying and received the surrender of more than forty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he sent Mobile Corps Commander Yang Jie to kill Yangqu bandit Yan Rulong; another commander subdued Lanxian bandit Gao Jiuying and took the surrender of more than forty stockades.

sentences.zh: 交城盜樑自雨、河曲盜李俊與九英犄角，國柱復分兵捕治。

translations.literal: The Jiaocheng bandits Liang Ziyu and the Hequ bandit Li Jun joined Jiuying in mutual support; Guozhu again divided troops to capture and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaocheng bandits Liang Ziyu and Hequ bandit Li Jun backed Jiuying; Guozhu sent divided forces against them.

sentences.zh: 國柱撫山西年餘，捕誅自成餘孽伏民間者，安集撫循，民漸復業。

translations.literal: Guozhu governed Shanxi for more than a year, capturing and executing Li Zicheng's remnant followers hidden among the people, comforting and soothing them, and the people gradually resumed their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in Shanxi he rooted out Li Zicheng's hidden followers, resettled the people, and farming gradually resumed.

sentences.zh: 客軍數往來，苦供億繁，國柱悉心措置，民不知兵。

translations.literal: Guest armies came and went frequently; the people suffered from heavy supply burdens, but Guozhu arranged matters with full care so the people scarcely felt the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Passing armies had burdened the people; Guozhu managed supplies so skillfully that civilians scarcely felt the troops.

sentences.zh: 十月，擢兼兵部侍郎，總督宣、大。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted to concurrent Vice Minister of War and governor-general of Xuan and Da.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and governor-general of Xuan-Datong.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，加兵部尚書，移督江南、江西、河南三行省。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year he was promoted to Minister of War and transferred to govern the three provinces of Jiangnan, Jiangxi, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year he became Minister of War and governor of Jiangnan, Jiangxi, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，安慶亂者馮洪圖陷巢縣，掠無為州，國柱令按察使土國寶從侍郎鄂屯帥師討之，獲洪圖及其黨蔣懋修、鍾武等。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year the rioter Feng Hongtu of Anqing seized Chaoxian and plundered Wuwei Prefecture; Guozhu ordered Surveillance Commissioner Tu Guobao to follow Vice Minister Etun in leading troops against him and captured Hongtu and his followers Jiang Maoxiu, Zhong Wu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, first month, Anqing rebel Feng Hongtu seized Chaoxian and looted Wuwei; Guozhu sent Surveillance Commissioner Tu Guobao with Vice Minister Etun, captured Hongtu, Jiang Maoxiu, Zhong Wu, and others.

sentences.zh: 江西總兵金聲桓叛，其將潘永禧犯徽州，國柱遣滿洲駐防官兵擊破之，复祁門、黟二縣。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Regional Commander Jin Shengheng rebelled; his general Pan Yongxi invaded Huizhou; Guozhu dispatched Manchu garrison troops to defeat him and recovered Qimen and Yi counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi commander Jin Shengheng rebelled, his general Pan Yongxi attacked Huizhou; Guozhu's Manchu garrison troops defeated him and recovered Qimen and Yi.

sentences.zh: 上命征南大將軍譚泰帥師討聲桓，克九江、南康、饒州等府。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Southern Expedition Grand General Tan Tai to lead troops against Shengheng and capture Jiujiang, Nanchang, Raozhou, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Grand General Tan Tai south; he took Jiujiang, Nanchang, Raozhou, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 明尚書餘應桂據都昌，出沒鄱陽湖，國柱令副將楊捷等從譚泰攻克都昌，獲應桂；

translations.literal: The Ming Minister Yu Yinggui held Duchang and raided Poyang Lake; Guozhu ordered Deputy General Yang Jie and others with Tan Tai to capture Duchang and take Yinggui;
translations.idiomatic: Ming minister Yu Yinggui held Duchang and raided Poyang Lake; Guozhu sent Deputy General Yang Jie with Tan Tai to take Duchang and capture Yinggui;

sentences.zh: 复擊敗其將鄧應龍等於武寧。

translations.literal: he again defeated his generals Deng Yinglong and others at Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: then defeated his generals Deng Yinglong and others at Wuning.

sentences.zh: 十月，廣東叛將李成棟自南雄侵贛州，國柱遣將與江西巡撫劉武元合兵擊殺之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Guangdong rebel general Li Chengdong invaded Ganzhou from Nanxiong; Guozhu dispatched generals to join Jiangxi Governor Liu Wuyuan in striking and killing him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Guangdong rebel Li Chengdong invaded Ganzhou from Nanxiong; Guozhu's generals joined Jiangxi Governor Liu Wuyuan and killed him.

sentences.zh: 六年，有王定安者，為亂於湖廣，陷羅田，結英山盜陳元等掠霍山，國柱遣中軍副將硃運亨等擊之，戰於三尖山，元等引去；

translations.literal: In the sixth year one Wang Ding'an made trouble in Huguang, seized Luotian, and joined the Yingshan bandit Chen Yuan and others in plundering Huoshan; Guozhu dispatched Headquarters Deputy General Zhu Yunheng and others against them; at Sanjian Mountain Yuan and the others withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Wang Ding'an rebelled in Huguang, took Luotian, and with Yingshan bandit Chen Yuan raided Huoshan; Zhu Yunheng drove them off at Sanjian Mountain;

sentences.zh: 又令總兵卜從善剿白雲、梅家、英窠諸寨。

translations.literal: he also ordered Regional Commander Bu Congshan to pacify the stockades at Baiyun, Meijia, and Yingwo.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Regional Commander Bu Congshan against the Baiyun, Meijia, and Yingwo stockades.

sentences.zh: 明石城王統錡率五千餘人自金紫寨赴援，倚山列陣，從善與戰，俘馘甚眾，獲所置總兵孔文燦、副將方學達等。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Shicheng Tongqi led more than five thousand men from the Jinzi Stockade to reinforce them, relying on the mountains to form battle lines; Congshan fought them, capturing and killing in great numbers and taking their appointed regional commander Kong Wencan and deputy general Fang Xueda.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Shicheng Tongqi brought five thousand men from Jinzi Stockade; Congshan defeated them, killed many, and captured rebel generals Kong Wencan and Fang Xueda.

sentences.zh: 國柱复率師會江寧昂邦章京巴山、提督張大猷討六安盜，圍將軍寨，擊斬其渠張福寰，降所置總兵王俊、副將霍維倫等。

translations.literal: Guozhu again led troops to join Jiangning Angbang Zhangjing Bashan and Provincial Commander Zhang Dayou in attacking the Lu'an bandits, besieging Jiangjun Stockade, striking and beheading the chieftain Zhang Fuhuan, and receiving the surrender of the appointed regional commander Wang Jun and deputy general Huo Weilun.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu joined Zhang Dayou and Bashan against Lu'an bandits, besieged Jiangjun Stockade, killed chief Zhang Fuhuan, and accepted the surrender of Wang Jun and Huo Weilun.

sentences.zh: 安徽境諸弄兵者，往往依山結寨相望，至是始盡。

translations.literal: Those who took up arms in Anhui often formed stockades on mountains facing one another; by this time they were all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui's mountain stockades were finally cleared.

sentences.zh: 明魯王以海在舟山，其將吳凱據大蘭山為聲援，上命國柱策剿撫。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai was at Zhoushan; his general Wu Kai held Mount Dalan as support; the sovereign ordered Guozhu to plan pacification and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai held Zhoushan; his general Wu Kai held Mount Dalan; the emperor ordered Guozhu to pacify or suppress them.

sentences.zh: 國柱知寧波諸生方聖時與以海臣嚴我公友，使為遊說，我公遂降，國柱護送京師。

translations.literal: Guozhu knew that the Ningbo licentiate Fang Shengshi was friendly with Yihai's minister Yan Wogong and had him conduct negotiations; Wogong then surrendered, and Guozhu escorted him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu sent Ningbo scholar Fang Shengshi, a friend of Yihai's minister Yan Wogong, to negotiate; Wogong surrendered and was escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上遣齎敕招凱，國柱复寓書焉，凱與其將顧奇勳、姜君獻、陳德芝等降。

translations.literal: The sovereign sent an envoy bearing an edict to summon Kai; Guozhu also sent a letter; Kai and his generals Gu Qixun, Jiang Junxian, Chen Dezhi, and others surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned Kai; Guozhu wrote as well, and Kai and his generals Gu Qixun, Jiang Junxian, and Chen Dezhi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 七年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，有張自盛者，為亂於福建，闌入江西境，保大覺岩，國柱檄提督劉光弼擊斬所置總兵李全等，遂獲自盛。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year Zhang Zisheng made trouble in Fujian, crossed into Jiangxi, and held Dajue Rock; Guozhu dispatched Provincial Commander Liu Guangbi to strike and behead the appointed regional commander Li Quan and others, then captured Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the seventh year Zhang Zisheng rebelled in Fujian, entered Jiangxi, and held Dajue Rock; Liu Guangbi killed rebel general Li Quan and captured Zisheng.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，明將張名振攻崇明、劉河、吳淞，國柱募水師，遣總兵王璟、副將張恩達分將之，敗之於靖江，复敗之於泰興，毀其舟，名振引去。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year the Ming general Zhang Mingzhen attacked Chongming, Liuhe, and Wusong; Guozhu recruited a naval force and dispatched Regional Commander Wang Jing and Deputy General Zhang Enda to command it, defeating Mingzhen at Jingjiang and again at Taixing, destroying his ships; Mingzhen withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, first month, Zhang Mingzhen attacked Chongming, Liuhe, and Wusong; Guozhu raised a fleet under Wang Jing and Zhang Enda, defeated him at Jingjiang and Taixing, destroyed his ships, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 二月，有賴龍者，為亂於湖廣，號「紅頭賊」，自桂東侵江西境，國柱與湖廣總督祖澤遠合兵攻桂東，得龍，亂乃定，復加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the second month one Lai Long made trouble in Huguang styled "Red-Head Bandits," invading Jiangxi from Guidong; Guozhu joined Huguang Governor-General Zu Zeyuan in attacking Guidong, captured Long, and the turmoil was settled; he was again promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Lai Long, the "Red-Head Bandit," invaded Jiangxi from Guidong; with Zu Zeyuan, Guozhu took Guidong, captured Long, and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 旋致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired.

sentences.zh: 國柱初至江南，駐防兵與民不相習，國柱善為撫戢，令行禁止，兵民相安。

translations.literal: When Guozhu first reached Jiangnan, the garrison troops and the people were unaccustomed to one another; Guozhu was skilled at soothing them, and orders were enforced and forbidden—soldiers and people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhu first reached Jiangnan, garrison troops and civilians were strangers to each other; he soothed both sides so that orders were obeyed and soldiers and people lived at peace.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of Kangxi year 3.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，舉人凡十六人，漢人習漢書者，齊國儒、硃燦然、羅綉錦、梁正大、雷興、馬國柱、金柱、王來用，得八人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong there were sixteen provincial graduates in all; of Han men who studied Han books, Qi Guoru, Zhu Ranran, Luo Xiujin, Liang Zhengda, Lei Xing, Ma Guozhu, Jin Zhu, and Wang Laiyong—eight obtained the degree.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong year 8 sixteen men passed the provincial examination; eight Han scholars of the classics passed, including Guozhu, Xiujin, and Xing.

sentences.zh: 國柱及繡錦、興、來用入關後，皆至督撫，而國柱、繡錦、興又同值文館。

translations.literal: Guozhu, Xiujin, Xing, and Laiyong, after entering the Pass, all reached the rank of governor or grand coordinator; Guozhu, Xiujin, and Xing had also served together in the Literary Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu, Xiujin, Xing, and Laiyong all rose to governorships after entering China; Guozhu, Xiujin, and Xing had served together in the Literary Institute.

sentences.zh: 繡錦，亦遼陽人，以諸生來歸。

translations.literal: Xiujin was also a native of Liaoyang and came over as a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujin, also from Liaoyang, had submitted as a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 天聰五年，與馬鳴佩同授工部啟心郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong he was appointed qixinlang in the Ministry of Works together with Ma Mingpei.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong year 5 he and Ma Mingpei were made qixinlang in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 六年，上以大凌河新附人眾，計國中無問官民，計口儲糧，有餘悉輸官，視市值記籍，徐為之償；

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because the people newly attached from Dalinghe were numerous, the state calculated that regardless of official or commoner, grain was to be stored by head count, with surplus all delivered to government stores, recorded in registers at market value, and repaid gradually;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, with many new subjects from Dalinghe, the court ordered every household to store grain by head count, deliver surplus to government stores at market value for gradual repayment;

sentences.zh: 有餘糧不輸者，許家人告發。

translations.literal: those with surplus grain who did not deliver might be reported by family members.
translations.idiomatic: families could report those who withheld surplus grain.

sentences.zh: 繡錦、鳴佩疏言：「民有餘糧，孰肯輸之官？

translations.literal: Xiujin and Mingpei memorialized, saying: "If the people have surplus grain, who will willingly deliver it to government stores?
translations.idiomatic: Xiujin and Mingpei wrote: "Who will voluntarily deliver surplus grain to the government?

sentences.zh: 縱令首告，有仇則訐，無仇則隱，所得必少。

translations.literal: Even if reporting is encouraged, with enmity there is accusation, without enmity concealment—the yield will surely be small.
translations.idiomatic: Encouraging informers yields little—enemies accuse, friends conceal.

sentences.zh: 且民不敢以糧入市，新人糧不足及舊人之無糧者，皆無所於糴。

translations.literal: Moreover the people dare not bring grain to market; newcomers lack grain and old subjects without grain have nowhere to buy.
translations.idiomatic: People will not bring grain to market; newcomers and the poor will have nothing to buy.

sentences.zh: 不若出令，無問滿、漢、蒙古官生軍民，人輸糧一斗。

translations.literal: Better issue an order: regardless of Manchu, Han, Mongol, official, student, soldier, or commoner, each person delivers one dou of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Better order every Manchu, Han, Mongol, official, student, soldier, and commoner to deliver one dou.

sentences.zh: 有糧者固易辦，無糧者人出銀二三錢，糴以輸官，亦無大損；

translations.literal: Those with grain can easily comply; those without can each pay two or three qian of silver, buy grain, and deliver it to government stores—no great harm;
translations.idiomatic: Those with grain can comply; those without can pay two or three qian of silver to buy grain—little hardship;

sentences.zh: 其有餘糧原輸官者，獎以升賞：此兩便之術也。」

translations.literal: those who originally had surplus grain and delivered it to government stores should be rewarded with promotion and bounty: this is a method benefiting both sides."
translations.idiomatic: reward those who voluntarily delivered surplus grain: that benefits everyone."

sentences.zh: 崇德元年五月，授內國史院學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Chongde he was appointed academician of the Inner Historiography Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde, fifth month, he was made academician of the Inner Historiography Academy.

sentences.zh: 纂太祖實錄成，得優賚。

translations.literal: When the compilation of the Taizu Veritable Records was completed he received special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu Veritable Records were completed he received special rewards.

sentences.zh: 漢軍旗制定，隸鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: When the Han banners were established he was enrolled in the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Bordered Blue Banner when the Han banners were organized.

sentences.zh: 七年，兼牛錄額真。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he concurrently served as niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he also served as niru commander.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關，七月，命以右副都御史，巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry into the Pass; in the seventh month he was ordered to serve as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he entered China; in the seventh month he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時李自成西走，其黨掠衛輝、懷慶間，而原武、新鄉諸縣盜競起。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng had fled west; his followers plundered between Weihui and Huaiqing, while bandits rose in competition in Yuanyang, Xinxiang, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had fled west; his followers raided Weihui and Huaiqing while bandits rose in Yuanyang, Xinxiang, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 繡錦至官，與總兵官祖可法等謀防禦。

translations.literal: Xiujin reached his post and with Regional Commander Zu Kefa and others planned defense.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujin took office and planned defense with Regional Commander Zu Kefa.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「自成之眾二萬餘，攻懷慶甚急。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Li Zicheng's force numbers more than twenty thousand and attacks Huaiqing urgently.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, saying: "Li Zicheng's force of more than twenty thousand is pressing Huaiqing hard.

sentences.zh: 明尚書張縉彥等擁兵河上，副將郭光輔、參將郝尚週不應徵調，叛而為寇。

translations.literal: The Ming Minister Zhang Jinyan and others hold troops on the river; Deputy General Guo Guangfu and Regimental Commander Hao Shangzhou do not respond to mobilization and have turned rebel to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ming minister Zhang Jinyan holds the river line while Guo Guangfu and Hao Shangzhou have defied orders and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 明兵在南，流寇在西，請發兵靖亂。」

translations.literal: Ming troops are in the south and roaming bandits in the west—please send troops to pacify the disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Ming armies are in the south and bandits in the west—send troops to pacify them."

sentences.zh: 上已令豫親王多鐸為定國大將軍，帥師南征，令取道河南捕治群寇。

translations.literal: The sovereign had already ordered Prince Regent Dodo as Great General Who Pacifies the State to lead a southern campaign and take the route through Henan to capture and punish the bandit hosts;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Regent Dodo had already been ordered south as Great General Who Pacifies the State, via Henan to suppress the bandits;

sentences.zh: 繡錦亦遣衛輝參將趙士忠等攻破婁兒寺盜寨，擒其渠。

translations.literal: Xiujin also dispatched Weihui Regimental Commander Zhao Shizhong and others to break the bandit stockade at Lou'er Temple and capture its chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujin sent Weihui commander Zhao Shizhong against the Lou'er Temple bandits and captured their chief.

sentences.zh: 繡錦請以河北荒地萬餘畝令守兵屯墾，得旨俞允。

translations.literal: Xiujin requested that more than ten thousand mu of wasteland north of the river be given to garrison troops for farming; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that ten thousand-plus mu of Hebei wasteland be farmed by garrison troops; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，擢兼兵部右侍郎，總督湖廣、四川。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year he was promoted to concurrent Right Vice Minister of War and governor-general of Huguang and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, eleventh month, he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and governor-general of Huguang and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 湖南諸州縣尚為明守，自成從子錦擁眾降於明，侵湖北。

translations.literal: Hunan prefectures and counties were still held by the Ming; Li Zicheng's nephew Jin led a host in surrender to the Ming and invaded Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan still held out for the Ming; Li Zicheng's nephew Jin led a large force that submitted to the Ming and invaded Hubei.

sentences.zh: 繡錦至荊州，錦率眾來攻。

translations.literal: Xiujin reached Jingzhou and Jin led his host to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiujin reached Jingzhou, Jin attacked.

sentences.zh: 順承郡王勒克德渾自江寧來援，錦敗走。

translations.literal: Prince of the Second Rank Leke Dehun came from Jiangning to reinforce; Jin was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Leke Dehun came from Jiangning to relieve him; Jin was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 勒克德渾師還，錦又至，繡錦帥師御之，錦复敗走。

translations.literal: When Leke Dehun's army returned, Jin came again; Xiujin led troops to meet him and Jin was again defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Leke Dehun withdrew, Jin returned; Xiujin defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 有胡公緒者，據天門八百洲，四出焚掠，戕署鹽道周世慶，繡錦遣中軍副將唐國臣、署總兵楊文富等分道討之，獲公緒，毀其巢。

translations.literal: One Hu Gongxu held the eight hundred isles of Tianmen, burning and plundering on all sides and killing Acting Salt Commissioner Zhou Shiqing; Xiujin dispatched Headquarters Deputy General Tang Guochen and Acting Regional Commander Yang Wenfu and others on separate routes to attack him, captured Gongxu, and destroyed his lair.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Gongxu held Tianmen's eight hundred isles, raided widely, and killed salt intendant Zhou Shiqing; Tang Guochen and Yang Wenfu destroyed his lair and captured him.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，遣總兵官徐勇擊破麻城山寨，獲其渠梅增、周文江；

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year he dispatched Regional Commander Xu Yong to break the Macheng mountain stockade and capture its chieftains Mei Zeng and Zhou Wenjiang;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, sixth month, Xu Yong broke the Macheng mountain stockade and captured chiefs Mei Zeng and Zhou Wenjiang;

sentences.zh: 岳州署總兵官高蛟龍等擊斬滿大壯，獲龍見明等。

translations.literal: Yuezhou Acting Regional Commander Gao Jiaolong and others struck and beheaded Man Dazhuang and captured Long Jianming and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhou acting commander Gao Jiaolong killed Man Dazhuang and captured Long Jianming.

sentences.zh: 九月，明總督何騰蛟寇岳州，繡錦遣將御之，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Ming Governor-General He Tengjiao attacked Yuezhou; Xiujin dispatched generals to meet him and beheaded and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Ming governor He Tengjiao attacked Yuezhou; Xiujin's generals defeated him with heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣總兵鄭四維等定夷陵、枝江、宜都三州縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he dispatched Regional Commander Zheng Siwei and others to settle the three prefectures of Yiling, Zhijiang, and Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zheng Siwei settled Yiling, Zhijiang, and Yidu.

sentences.zh: 四年，定南大將軍恭順王孔有德等略湖廣，取長沙、衡州、寶慶、辰州諸府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Prince of the South Who Pacifies Kong Youde and others advanced on Huguang and took Changsha, Hengzhou, Baoqing, Chenzhou, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Prince Who Pacifies the South Kong Youde took Changsha, Hengzhou, Baoqing, Chenzhou, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 繡錦條奏增設鎮協，下部議行。

translations.literal: Xiujin memorialized item by item requesting added garrisons and coordinated commands; the ministries approved and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujin memorialized for added garrisons; the ministries approved.

sentences.zh: 王光泰以鄖陽叛，上命侍郎喀喀木帥師討之，繡錦與合兵克鄖陽，光泰走四川。

translations.literal: Wang Guangtai rebelled at Yunyang; the sovereign ordered Vice Minister Kakamu to lead troops against him; Xiujin joined forces to capture Yunyang and Guangtai fled to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangtai rebelled at Yunyang; Kakamu and Xiujin took the city and Guangtai fled to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 五年，金聲桓以江西叛，湖南騷動，常德、武岡、辰、沅諸府州復入於明。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Jin Shengheng rebelled in Jiangxi; Hunan was disturbed and Changde, Wugang, Chen, and Yuan prefectures returned to the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Jin Shengheng rebelled in Jiangxi; Hunan was shaken and Changde, Wugang, Chen, and Yuan returned to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 繡錦疏留喀喀木駐荊州，而分遣總兵徐勇、馬蛟麟等分守要隘，屢敗明將馬進忠等。

translations.literal: Xiujin memorialized to retain Kakamu at Jingzhou while separately dispatching Regional Commanders Xu Yong, Ma Jiaolin, and others to hold key passes, repeatedly defeating Ming generals such as Ma Jinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujin kept Kakamu at Jingzhou and sent Xu Yong and Ma Jiaolin to hold the passes, repeatedly defeating Ming general Ma Jinzhong.

sentences.zh: 上復命鄭親王濟爾哈朗共率師徇湖南，漸收諸郡縣。

translations.literal: The sovereign again ordered Prince of the First Rank Jirhalang to lead troops jointly into Hunan, gradually recovering prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jirhalang was again ordered into Hunan and gradually recovered the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 繡錦疏請移降卒腹地，毋使師還後復為餘孽煽誘，上嘉納其言。

translations.literal: Xiujin memorialized requesting that surrendered soldiers be moved inland lest, after the army withdrew, remnants be incited to rebel; the sovereign praised and accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujin asked that surrendered troops be resettled inland lest they rebel after the army withdrew; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year he died and was posthumously given the rank of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the seventh year and was posthumously made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 弟繪錦，自通政司理事官再遷，終貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: His younger brother Huixin rose from supervising official in the Office of Transmission to end as governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Huixin rose from the Office of Transmission to governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 興，亦遼東人。

translations.literal: Xing was also a native of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was also from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，以諸生選直文館。

translations.literal: In the Taizu Emperor's time he was chosen as a licentiate to serve in the Literary Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taizu Emperor he was chosen as a licentiate for the Literary Institute.

sentences.zh: 事太宗，授秘書院副理事官。

translations.literal: Serving the Taizong, he was appointed vice supervising official of the Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Hong Taiji, he became vice supervising official of the Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 崇德間，遷都察院理事官。

translations.literal: During the Chongde period he was transferred to supervising official of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongde era he became a Censorate supervising official.

sentences.zh: 漢軍旗制定，隸正黃旗。

translations.literal: When the Han banners were established he was enrolled in the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Plain Yellow Banner when the Han banners were organized.

sentences.zh: 順治元年十月，命以右副都御史巡撫天津。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Shunzhi he was ordered to serve as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi, tenth month, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 李聯芳、張成軒為亂滄州、南皮間，興與總兵官婁光先帥師討之。

translations.literal: Li Lianfang and Zhang Chengxuan were bandits between Cangzhou and Nanpi; Xing with Regional Commander Lou Guangxian led troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lianfang and Zhang Chengxuan raided Cangzhou and Nanpi; Xing and Lou Guangxian campaigned against them.

sentences.zh: 成軒等將遁出海，師已扼海口，乃驚潰，投水死者強半。

translations.literal: Chengxuan and the others were about to flee to sea, but the army had already blocked the harbor mouth; they panicked and collapsed, and more than half drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxuan tried to flee by sea but the harbor was blocked; his men panicked and more than half drowned.

sentences.zh: 興復遣兵捕治，斬渠宥脅，盜盡散。

translations.literal: Xing again dispatched troops to capture and punish them, beheading the chieftains and sparing the compelled followers; the bandits all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Xing sent troops again, executed the chiefs, spared followers, and dispersed the band.

sentences.zh: 疏言大沽海口為神京門戶，請置戰船為備，下所司議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the Dagu estuary was the gateway to the sacred capital and requested warships for defense; the responsible offices approved and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for warships to guard the Dagu estuary, the capital's gateway; the order was approved.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，移巡撫陝西。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year he was transferred to grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, second month, he was transferred to governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 陝西方被兵，民多流亡，興招徠撫綏，疏述其狀。

translations.literal: Shaanxi had just suffered from warfare; many people were fugitives; Xing recruited and comforted them and memorialized describing the situation.
translations.idiomatic: War-ravaged Shaanxi had many refugees; Xing recruited and comforted them and reported their condition.

sentences.zh: 上旌以冠服、裘馬。

translations.literal: The sovereign rewarded him with ceremonial robes and fur horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with ceremonial dress and horses.

sentences.zh: 三年，肅親王豪格帥師自陝西徇四川，師未至，有孫守法者，為亂於興安；

translations.literal: In the third year Prince Su Hoge led troops from Shaanxi into Sichuan; before the army arrived, Sun Shoufa made trouble in Xing'an;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Prince Su Hoge marched from Shaanxi into Sichuan; before he arrived, Sun Shoufa rebelled in Xing'an;

sentences.zh: 賀珍又以漢中叛。

translations.literal: He Zhen also rebelled at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhen rebelled at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 興移潼關兵戍商州，密檄漢羌道胡全才為備，待師至，悉戡定。

translations.literal: Xing moved Tongguan troops to garrison Shangzhou and secretly ordered the Han-Qiang Circuit intendant Hu Quancai to prepare; when the army arrived, all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xing shifted Tongguan troops to Shangzhou and ordered Han-Qiang intendant Hu Quancai to prepare; when the army came, both rebellions were crushed.

sentences.zh: 興疏請隴州置兵，臨洮、鞏昌留屯軍防邊，皆報可。

translations.literal: Xing memorialized requesting troops at Longzhou and garrison farming at Lintao and Gongchang to guard the frontier—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for troops at Longzhou and farming garrisons at Lintao and Gongchang; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，以疾乞罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, on grounds of illness, he requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, fourth month, he retired for illness.

sentences.zh: 十年八月，復起巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year he was again recalled as grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, eighth month, he was recalled as governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 未上，卒，贈兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he died and was posthumously given the rank of Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking office and was posthumously made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 來用，亦隸鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: Laiyong was also enrolled in the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Laiyong also belonged to the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 授工部啟心郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed qixinlang in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made qixinlang in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 順治初，再遷山西布政使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he was twice promoted to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he rose to Provincial Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 三年，師略四川，三月，授來用戶部右侍郎，總督山西、川、陝糧餉，駐西安。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the army advanced on Sichuan, in the third month Laiyong was appointed Right Vice Minister of Revenue and made governor of grain supplies for Shanxi, Sichuan, and Shaanxi, stationed at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, as armies advanced on Sichuan, he was made Right Vice Minister of Revenue and grain governor for Shanxi, Sichuan, and Shhanxi at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 疏言陝西兵後民困，請蠲荒徵熟。

translations.literal: He memorialized that after warfare the people of Shaanxi were afflicted and requested exemption of tax on wasteland while collecting on cultivated land.
translations.idiomatic: He reported Shaanxi's postwar distress and asked to tax only cultivated land, not wasteland.

sentences.zh: 山西銅缺，鑄錢多，定值過低，商不前，請酌增。

translations.literal: Shanxi lacked copper; too much coin was cast and its fixed value was too low, so merchants would not come—he requested moderate increase.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi lacked copper, too much coin was cast at too low a rate, and trade stalled—he asked for adjustment.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言漢南遘賀珍亂，蹂躪荒殘，請恩賑，並敕部儲備肅親王還師餉糈。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized that southern Han suffered He Zhen's rebellion and was trampled into desolation, requesting gracious relief, and also ordered the ministry to store provisions for Prince Su's returning army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he reported southern Shaanxi ravaged by He Zhen and asked for relief and stores for Prince Su's returning army.

sentences.zh: 五年，疏言河西回亂，運河阻，諸軍南討，請發湖廣漕供餉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized that the Hexi Muslims were in turmoil, the Grand Canal was blocked, and southern campaigns needed grain—he requested Huguang grain transport for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he reported Muslim unrest in Hexi, blockage of the Grand Canal, and asked for Huguang grain for southern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 又言漢中屯軍歲餉數十萬，請專設餉司。

translations.literal: He also said Hanzhong garrison troops required hundreds of thousands in annual pay and requested a dedicated pay office.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Hanzhong garrisons needed hundreds of thousands in annual pay and asked for a dedicated pay office.

sentences.zh: 皆如所請。

translations.literal: All were granted as he requested.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏言兵出鎮，贍其孥如所食糈。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized that when troops went out to garrison posts, their wives and children should be provisioned with grain as the soldiers were.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he asked that when troops garrisoned the frontier, their families receive the same grain ration as the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 司兵者請自離伍日起，司餉者請自到軍日起，持異議，請定例畫一。

translations.literal: The military office requested counting from the day of leaving the ranks; the pay office requested counting from the day of reaching the army—each held a different view, and he asked that a single regulation be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The military office wanted rations from the day men left the rolls; the pay office from the day they reached camp—he asked for one rule.

sentences.zh: 部議以應徵日起，中途逃亡，不得濫與。

translations.literal: The ministry decided from the day of mobilization; those who fled en route should not be given rations indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled from mobilization day; deserters en route would not receive rations.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，御史聶玠劾來用專倚中軍王楨，自隳職業，部議左遷，援赦免。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year Censor Nie Jie impeached Laiyong for relying solely on headquarters officer Wang Zhen and neglecting his duties; the ministry proposed demotion, but amnesty excused it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, first month, Censor Nie Jie impeached Laiyong for relying on headquarters officer Wang Zhen; demotion was proposed but amnesty excused it.

sentences.zh: 七月，裁缺。

translations.literal: In the seventh month his post was abolished in the retrenchment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month his post was cut in retrenchment.

sentences.zh: 九年，命巡撫順天。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed governor of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 十年，移駐河間。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he moved his headquarters to Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he moved his headquarters to Hejian.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以定南王孔有德喪歸，其屬吏或格詔書不出迎，坐左遷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when Prince Who Pacifies the South Kong Youde returned for mourning, some of his subordinate officials obstructed the edict and did not go out to receive him; for this Laiyong was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year some of Prince Who Pacifies the South Kong Youde's subordinates refused to receive him on his return from mourning; Laiyong was demoted.

sentences.zh: 十四年，改授河南大樑道。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was reassigned to the Daliang Circuit of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was reassigned to Henan's Daliang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 丁文盛，廣寧人。

translations.literal: Ding Wensheng was a native of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wensheng was from Guangning.

sentences.zh: 初為明諸生。

translations.literal: At first he was a licentiate under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a Ming licentiate.

sentences.zh: 天命六年，歸太祖。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianming he submitted to the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming year 6 he submitted to the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 天聰間，授兵部啟心郎。

translations.literal: During the Tiancong period he was appointed qixinlang in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancong era he was made qixinlang in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，偕同官趙福星疏言：「師行戒毋擾民，子女玉帛，秋毫無犯，但發倉庫以佐軍興。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year he joined his colleague Zhao Fuxing in memorializing: "On campaign, warn against disturbing the people; in women, children, silk, and treasure let not the slightest be violated, but issue from storehouses to assist military needs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, first month, he and Zhao Fuxing wrote: "On campaign do not disturb the people; take nothing in women, children, silk, or treasure, but draw from storehouses to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 攻關東八城，當先其易者，後其難者。

translations.literal: In attacking the eight cities east of the passes, take the easy ones first and the hard ones later.
translations.idiomatic: Attack the eight eastern pass cities in order of ease, not difficulty.

sentences.zh: 舍寧、錦、前衛，但得其他小城，因糧以度師，進攻山海。

translations.literal: Leave Ningyuan, Jinzhou, and the forward guard, but take the other small cities and use their grain to sustain the army, then advance on Shanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Leave Ningyuan, Jinzhou, and the forward guard; seize the lesser towns, live off their grain, then strike Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 舊制編民為兵，十丁而取一。

translations.literal: The old system registered commoners as soldiers, taking one from ten adult males.
translations.idiomatic: The old rule drafted one man in ten.

sentences.zh: 當令諸甲喇及領屯將吏，慎選年事盛強、身家相稱者，毋許以他人代。

translations.literal: Each jalan and the garrison-farming officers should carefully choose men in their prime whose age and household standing match, and not permit substitutes.
translations.idiomatic: Each banner and farming officer should choose able men of proper standing, not substitutes.

sentences.zh: 永平砲兵衣食不足，宜擇其技精者授千總，督演習，食糈視鑄砲之工。

translations.literal: Yongping artillerymen lack food and clothing; choose the most skilled among them and appoint them as chiliarchs to supervise drill, with grain equal to cannon-casting workers.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping gunners lack food and clothing; appoint the best as chiliarchs to drill them and pay them like cannon founders.

sentences.zh: 哈喇沁降者置遼河外，慮且逃亡，宜移屯腹地。」

translations.literal: The surrendered Khalkha placed beyond the Liao River may yet flee; they should be moved to garrison the interior."
translations.idiomatic: Khalkha surrendered beyond the Liao may flee; move them inland."

translations.literal: (Their memorial closed.)
translations.idiomatic: (Their memorial closed.)

sentences.zh: 及孔有德。

translations.literal: When Kong Youde
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Youde

sentences.zh: 耿仲明來降，五月，文盛、福星上疏請水陸並進，攻山海，取旅順；

translations.literal: and Geng Zhongming came over, in the fifth month Wensheng and Fuxing memorialized requesting advance by land and water, attacking Shanhai and taking Lushun;
translations.idiomatic: and Geng Zhongming submitted, in the fifth month Wensheng and Fuxing asked for a combined land and sea attack on Shanhaiguan and Lushun;

sentences.zh: 並言：「毛帥來歸，令金、漢官吏出羊、雞、鵝、米、肉以贍其兵。

translations.literal: they also said: "If Commander Mao comes over, order Manchu and Han officials to provide sheep, chickens, geese, rice, and meat to provision his troops.
translations.idiomatic: they also said: "If Commander Mao submits, have Manchu and Han officials supply his troops with sheep, fowl, rice, and meat.

sentences.zh: 臣慮新人未必肥，而舊人已不勝瘠。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the newcomers may not be well fed while the old subjects are already too lean.
translations.idiomatic: New subjects may not be well fed while old subjects are already thin.

sentences.zh: 復使市馬，力尤不能舉。

translations.literal: If they are also made to buy horses, their strength especially cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing them to buy horses is beyond their strength.

sentences.zh: 若用八門稅，一二月已足。」

translations.literal: If the eight-gate taxes are used, one or two months would suffice."
translations.idiomatic: The eight-gate taxes would suffice in a month or two."

sentences.zh: 孔有德等，毛文龍部曲，文龍嘗使冒其姓，故是時猶稱毛帥。

translations.literal: Kong Youde and the others were Mao Wenlong's subordinates; Wenlong once had them use his surname, hence they were still called Commander Mao at that time.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Youde and the others had been Mao Wenlong's men; Wenlong had let them use his surname, so they were still called Commander Mao.

sentences.zh: 及旅順既下，七月，文盛、福星復請城旅順，加意防守。

translations.literal: After Lushun was taken, in the seventh month Wensheng and Fuxing again requested fortifying Lushun with special attention to defense.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushun fell, in the seventh month Wensheng and Fuxing asked that Lushun be fortified and strongly garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 考績，授世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: At merit review he was granted the hereditary office of niru zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: At merit review he received the hereditary office of niru captain.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關，授山東登萊兵備道參政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the entry into the Pass and was appointed vice commissioner of the Deng-Lai military defense circuit of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shunzhi he entered China and was made vice commissioner of Shandong's Deng-Lai military circuit.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，授右僉都御史，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, sixth month, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 濰縣盜張廣為亂，以數千人攻萊州，文盛令游擊馮武鄉等討之，戰三埠，再戰紅山口，斬廣黨尼思齊、趙明春。

translations.literal: The Weixian bandit Zhang Guang made trouble with several thousand men attacking Laizhou; Wensheng ordered Mobile Corps Commander Feng Wuxiang and others against him; they fought at Sanbu and again at Hongshankou, beheading Guang's followers Ni Siqi and Zhao Mingchun.
translations.idiomatic: Weixian bandit Zhang Guang led thousands against Laizhou; Feng Wuxiang defeated him at Sanbu and Hongshankou and killed Ni Siqi and Zhao Mingchun.

sentences.zh: 廣走平度，游擊楊遇明逐之，及於徐裡甿，射廣殪，殲其徒。

translations.literal: Guang fled to Pingdu; Mobile Corps Commander Yang Yuming pursued him to Xulimeng and shot Guang dead, annihilating his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Guang fled to Pingdu; Yang Yuming pursued him to Xulimeng, shot him dead, and destroyed his band.

sentences.zh: 明季馬政弛，驛馬缺，求諸民，文盛疏請以餘存驛站銀市馬。

translations.literal: In late Ming the horse administration was lax, post horses were lacking, and they were sought from the people; Wensheng memorialized requesting use of surplus post-station silver to buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: Late-Ming horse administration had collapsed; Wensheng asked to buy post horses with surplus station silver.

sentences.zh: 明季增牙稅及他雜稅，文盛疏請罷。

translations.literal: Late Ming had added tooth taxes and other miscellaneous levies; Wensheng memorialized requesting their abolition.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to abolish late-Ming tooth taxes and miscellaneous levies.

sentences.zh: 臨清、東昌、平山諸衛置兵五千人，虛額逾半，文盛疏請減，留二千人，節餉令州縣募壯丁逐捕盜賊。

translations.literal: Linqing, Dongchang, and Pingshan guards had five thousand troops on paper with more than half empty slots; Wensheng memorialized requesting reduction to two thousand men, saving pay and letting prefectures and counties recruit stout men to hunt bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Linqing, Dongchang, and Pingshan guards listed five thousand troops, half phantom slots; he cut them to two thousand and had counties recruit men to hunt bandits.

sentences.zh: 別疏又請教有司清刑獄，禁獄卒毋虐囚。

translations.literal: In another memorial he again requested that officials be taught to clear criminal cases and jailers forbidden to torture prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked officials to clear criminal cases and forbid jailers to torture prisoners.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were sent to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved by the ministries.

sentences.zh: 三年，盜發茌平、高唐諸縣，文盛請兵，上遣副都統覺善率師捕治。

translations.literal: In the third year bandits rose in Chiping, Gaotang, and other counties; Wensheng requested troops and the sovereign dispatched Vice Commander Jueshan to lead troops in capture and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year bandits rose in Chiping and Gaotang; the emperor sent Vice Commander Jueshan against them.

sentences.zh: 四年，文盛被彈事不勝任，左遷河南按察使，稍遷福建布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wensheng was impeached as incompetent and demoted to Henan Surveillance Commissioner, later transferred to Fujian Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was impeached as incompetent, demoted to Henan surveillance commissioner, and later made Fujian provincial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 文盛子思孔，字景行。

translations.literal: Wensheng's son Sicong, style Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng's son Sicong, courtesy name Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the ninth year of Shunzhi, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi year 9 jinshi, he became a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 四遷，授陝西漢羌道副使，康熙二年，巡撫賈漢复劾思孔追胥役蝕糧草逾限，左遷河南開封府同知。

translations.literal: After four promotions he was appointed vice commissioner of the Han-Qiang Circuit of Shaanxi; in the second year of Kangxi Governor Jia Hanfu impeached Sicong for runner extortion and embezzling fodder beyond the limit, and he was demoted to vice prefect of Kaifeng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he became vice commissioner of Shaanxi's Han-Qiang Circuit; in Kangxi year 2 Governor Jia Hanfu impeached him for runner extortion and fodder embezzlement, and he was demoted to Kaifeng vice prefect.

sentences.zh: 思孔詣通政使自列胥役蝕糧草，獄瘐家罄。

translations.literal: Sicong went to the Office of Transmission to state in person that runners had embezzled fodder and the case had ruined his family.
translations.idiomatic: Sicong told the Office of Transmission that runners had embezzled fodder and ruined his family.

sentences.zh: 事上巡撫，巡撫久乃入告未嘗逾限，下總督白如梅勘實。

translations.literal: The matter went up to the governor, who long afterward reported that he had never exceeded the limit; investigation was sent to Governor-General Bai Rumei, who verified the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The governor eventually reported no overrun; Governor-General Bai Rumei verified it.

sentences.zh: 复授直隸通薊道。

translations.literal: He was again appointed to the Tong-Ji Circuit of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to Zhili's Tong-Ji Circuit.

sentences.zh: 直隸未設布政、按察兩司，八年，巡撫金世德請增置保定守道領錢穀，以授思孔。

translations.literal: Zhili had not yet established provincial administration and surveillance commissions; in the eighth year Governor Jin Shide requested adding a Baoding circuit intendant to oversee revenue and grain, and Sicong was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili lacked provincial commissioners; in year 8 Governor Jin Shide created a Baoding intendant for revenue and appointed Sicong.

sentences.zh: 再遷江南布政使。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Jiangnan provincial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂亂方定，師行江西、湖廣，思孔主餽運，應期不愆。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Sangui's rebellion had just been settled and armies marched through Jiangxi and Huguang; Sicong managed supply transport and met every deadline.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Sangui's rebellion, armies marched through Jiangxi and Huguang; Sicong supplied them on time.

sentences.zh: 禁旅還自福建，庀役具舟，科量悉當。

translations.literal: When the banner troops returned from Fujian he arranged boats and measured loads—all were proper.
translations.idiomatic: When banner troops returned from Fujian he furnished boats and measured cargoes correctly.

sentences.zh: 修蘇州府學，置育嬰堂、養濟院，諸政皆舉。

translations.literal: He restored the Suzhou Prefecture school, established foundling halls and poorhouses, and in all policies acted thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Suzhou's prefectural school, founded foundling halls and poorhouses, and governed thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遇大計，總督於成龍以思孔督賦未中程，不得舉卓異，特疏薦廉能，上命準卓異。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, at the great assessment, Governor-General Yu Chenglong said Sicong had not met the revenue target and could not be nominated for outstanding merit, but specially memorialized him as incorrupt and capable; the sovereign ordered outstanding merit approved.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21, at the great assessment, Yu Chenglong said Sicong missed the revenue target but specially recommended him as incorrupt and capable; the emperor approved outstanding merit.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢偏沅巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to governor of Bian-Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he was promoted to governor of Bian-Yuan.

sentences.zh: 偏沅所領七郡，溪山環互，民、僚雜處，反側初定，餘孽每煽亂，思孔撫其渠，群盜漸散。

translations.literal: The seven prefectures of Bian-Yuan were ringed by streams and mountains with Han and Liao peoples mixed; rebellion had just been settled and remnants often stirred trouble; Sicong soothed the chieftains and the bandit hosts gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Bian-Yuan's seven prefectures mixed Han and Liao in rugged country; Sicong pacified chiefs and bandits gradually dispersed.

sentences.zh: 复岳麓書院，御書旌楣。

translations.literal: He restored the Yuelu Academy and received an imperial inscription for its gate.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Yuelu Academy and received an imperial inscription for its gate.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，移撫河南，方上，而有夏逢龍之亂，复移撫湖北。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to govern Henan; before he arrived Xia Fenglong rebelled, and he was again transferred to govern Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he was transferred to Henan; before arriving, Xia Fenglong rebelled and he was sent to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 逢龍私自署置千總胡耀乾，參將李廷秀，馬兵周凱、萬金鎰皆號總兵，守備林德號副將。

translations.literal: Fenglong had on his own appointed Regiment Commander Hu Yaogan, Regimental Commander Li Tingxiu, and cavalry officers Zhou Kai and Wan Jinyi all styled regional commanders, and Garrison Commander Lin De styled deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Fenglong had styled Hu Yaogan, Li Tingxiu, Zhou Kai, and Wan Jinyi as regional commanders and Lin De as deputy general.

sentences.zh: 上命振武將軍瓦岱帥師討之，趣思孔詣荊州主餉。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Pacifying Martial General Wadai to lead troops against him and urged Sicong to go to Jingzhou to manage supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered General Wadai against him and urged Sicong to Jingzhou to manage supplies.

sentences.zh: 思孔以武昌倉庫皆陷賊，諸軍餉乏，乃發河南庫帑，護詣襄陽，諸軍資以濟，疏報稱旨。

translations.literal: Sicong, because Wuchang's storehouses had all fallen to the rebels and the armies lacked pay, issued grain from Henan's treasury, escorted it to Xiangyang, and the armies were thereby sustained; his memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: With Wuchang's stores in rebel hands, Sicong drew on Henan's treasury, escorted grain to Xiangyang, and saved the armies; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 七月，瓦岱師至，蹙賊黃州，誅逢龍，而耀乾等尚據武昌拒命。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wadai's army arrived, pressed the rebels at Huangzhou, executed Fenglong, but Yaogan and the others still held Wuchang in defiance.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wadai pressed the rebels at Huangzhou and killed Fenglong, but Yaogan still held Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 思孔至漢口，具舟渡江，單騎叩漢陽門，呼耀乾出見，耀乾等遂降。

translations.literal: Sicong reached Hankou, prepared boats to cross the river, and alone on horseback knocked at the Hanyang Gate, calling Yaogan out to meet him; Yaogan and the others then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Sicong reached Hankou, crossed alone on horseback to the Hanyang Gate, summoned Yaogan, and secured his surrender.

sentences.zh: 思孔入武昌，數耀乾等罪而誅之，並戮所置巡撫傅爾學、布政婁方順、驛道金奇功，凡八人，武昌遂定。

translations.literal: Sicong entered Wuchang, counted Yaogan's crimes and executed him, and also executed the appointed governor Fu Erxue, provincial commissioner Lou Fangshun, courier intendant Jin Qigong, eight men in all; Wuchang was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuchang he condemned and executed Yaogan, rebel governor Fu Erxue, commissioner Lou Fangshun, intendant Jin Qigong, and eight others; Wuchang was secured.

sentences.zh: 九月，復設湖廣總督，以命思孔。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Huguang governor-general was re-established and Sicong was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Huguang governor-general was restored and Sicong was appointed.

sentences.zh: 陳龍越八者，逢龍之徒也，二十八年五月，謀為變，期夜半。

translations.literal: Chen Long and eight others were Fenglong's followers; in the fifth month of the twenty-eighth year they plotted revolt at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Long and eight others, Fenglong's followers, plotted revolt at midnight in the fifth month of year 28.

sentences.zh: 思孔晡始聞，執陳龍越八戮於市，他悉不問。

translations.literal: Sicong heard only in late afternoon, seized Chen Long and the eight others and executed them in the market; the rest were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Sicong learned late in the day, seized Chen Long and eight others, executed them publicly, and questioned no one else.

sentences.zh: 設水師，分戍武昌、荊州、岳州、常德。

translations.literal: He established a naval force and divided garrisons at Wuchang, Jingzhou, Yuezhou, and Changde.
translations.idiomatic: He established a navy and garrisoned Wuchang, Jingzhou, Yuezhou, and Changde.

sentences.zh: 嘗歲饑，便宜發帑市米江西，平值以糴。

translations.literal: Once in a famine year he expediently issued treasury funds to buy rice in Jiangxi and sold it at fair price.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he issued treasury funds to buy Jiangxi rice and sold it at fair price.

sentences.zh: 三十三年四月，移督雲、貴。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirty-third year he was transferred to govern Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 33, he was transferred to Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 祝世昌，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shichang was a native of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shichang was from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 先世在明初授遼陽定邊前衛世襲指揮，十數傳至世昌，為鎮江城游擊。

translations.literal: His forebears in the early Ming were granted hereditary command of the Liaoyang Dingbian Forward Guard; after more than ten generations Shichang became mobile corps commander of Zhenjiang City.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had held hereditary command of Liaoyang's Dingbian Forward Guard for generations; Shichang became mobile corps commander of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 天命六年，太祖克遼陽，世昌率三百餘人來降，仍授游擊，統其眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianming, when the Taizu Emperor captured Liaoyang, Shichang led more than three hundred men to surrender and was still appointed mobile corps commander to command his host.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming year 6, when the Taizu Emperor took Liaoyang, Shichang surrendered with three hundred men and remained mobile corps commander over them.

sentences.zh: 命董築瀋陽、遼陽、海州三城，事竟，授瀋陽城守昂邦章京。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise the building of the three cities of Shenyang, Liaoyang, and Haizhou; when the work was done he was appointed angbang zhangjing defending Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised construction of Shenyang, Liaoyang, and Haizhou; when finished he was made angbang zhangjing of Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 天聰五年，從征大凌河。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong he followed the campaign against Dalinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong year 5 he campaigned against Dalinghe.

sentences.zh: 六年，太宗閱烏真超哈兵，賚諸將，世昌與焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Taizong reviewed the musket troops and rewarded the generals; Shichang was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hong Taiji reviewed musket troops and rewarded the generals, including Shichang.

sentences.zh: 尋遷禮部承政，授世職參將。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Rites and granted the hereditary office of regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Rites and received the hereditary rank of regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，克旅順。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year Lushun was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year Lushun was taken.

sentences.zh: 世昌疏請大舉伐明，謂：「攻城當專用紅衣砲，國中新舊三十餘具，瀋陽留四具，城守已足，餘悉載軍中。

translations.literal: Shichang memorialized requesting a great campaign against the Ming, saying: "In storming cities one should rely exclusively on red-barrel cannon; in the state there are more than thirty old and new pieces—leave four at Shenyang, enough for city defense, and load the rest on the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang asked for a major Ming campaign, writing: "Siege requires red-barrel cannon; keep four at Shenyang and send the rest with the army.

sentences.zh: 砲多則糜藥亦多，藥局製藥，硝丁淋硝慮不足於用。

translations.literal: Many cannon consume much powder; the powder works make powder, and saltpeter workers leach saltpeter—there is fear it will not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Many guns need much powder; the powder works may not keep up.

sentences.zh: 旅順新獲硝磺，宜以其半送瀋陽製藥。

translations.literal: The saltpeter and sulfur newly taken at Lushun—half should be sent to Shenyang for making powder.
translations.idiomatic: Send half the saltpeter and sulfur taken at Lushun to Shenyang for powder.

sentences.zh: 師行克城邑，當得練達謹慎之吏，不求小利，不貪財賄，乃能戢民心、保疆圉，宜預選令從軍備任使。

translations.literal: On campaign, when cities and towns are taken, experienced and cautious officials should be obtained who do not seek petty profit or covet bribes—only then can popular hearts be restrained and the frontier preserved; such men should be chosen in advance to follow the army for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Choose prudent officials who do not seek petty gain to govern captured towns and preserve the frontier.

sentences.zh: 用兵當兼奇正，輕兵先發，奪人畜，掠儲峙，然後整軍挾紅衣砲自大道徐進。」

translations.literal: In using troops one should combine orthodox and unorthodox methods: light troops go first to seize livestock and plunder stores, then the main army with red-barrel cannon advances slowly on the great road."
translations.idiomatic: Combine orthodox and surprise tactics: light troops seize livestock and stores, then the main army with red-barrel guns advances on the highway."

sentences.zh: 上尋遣貝勒阿巴泰等將二千人略山海關外，未深入，引還。

translations.literal: The sovereign soon dispatched Prince Abatai and others with two thousand men to raid beyond Shanhaiguan without penetrating deeply, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The khan soon sent Prince Abatai with two thousand men to raid beyond Shanhaiguan without penetrating deeply.

sentences.zh: 崇德七年，疏請禁俘良家婦鬻入樂戶，上諭都察院承政張存仁、祖可法曰：「世昌豈不知朕禁樂戶？

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongde he memorialized requesting prohibition of selling captive women of good families into music households; the sovereign instructed Censorate Ministers Zhang Cunren and Zu Kefa: "Does Shichang not know that I forbid music households?
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde year 7 he asked to forbid selling captive women of good families to music households; the khan told censors Zhang Cunren and Zu Kefa: "Does Shichang not know I forbid music households?

sentences.zh: 而為此疏，不過徇漢人，藉此要譽耳。

translations.literal: Yet he makes this memorial—nothing more than currying favor with Han people and seeking reputation thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He writes this only to curry favor with Han subjects and win praise.

sentences.zh: 朕度世昌身在我國，心猶鄉明。

translations.literal: I judge that though Shichang's body is in our state, his heart still inclines to his native Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lives in our state, his heart still inclines to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 世昌果忠於明，明以元功臣田、劉、張三姓之裔隸樂戶，世昌何不聞有言乎？

translations.literal: If Shichang were truly loyal to the Ming, the Ming made descendants of the Yuan meritorious families Tian, Liu, and Zhang into music households—why did Shichang never hear any protest?
translations.idiomatic: If he were loyal to the Ming, why did he never protest when the Ming enslaved Yuan meritorious families Tian, Liu, and Zhang as music households?

sentences.zh: 朕視滿、蒙、漢若一體，爾等同心輔國。

translations.literal: I regard Manchu, Mongol, and Han as one body; you should assist the state with one heart.
translations.idiomatic: I treat Manchu, Mongol, and Han as one; serve the state with one heart.

sentences.zh: 譬諸五味，貴調劑得宜。

translations.literal: It is like the five flavors—all depend on proper blending.
translations.idiomatic: Like the five flavors, all depend on proper blending.

sentences.zh: 若各相庇護，是猶咸苦酸辛不得其和。

translations.literal: If each protects his own, it is like salty, bitter, sour, and pungent failing to harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: If each protects his own, flavors cannot harmonize.

sentences.zh: 爾等徇世昌而不舉劾，咎在爾等。

translations.literal: You curry favor with Shichang and do not impeach—the fault lies with you.
translations.idiomatic: You favor Shichang and do not impeach—the fault is yours.

sentences.zh: 曾子曰：'吾日三省吾身。

translations.literal: Zengzi said: 'Each day I examine myself three times.
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi said: 'Each day I examine myself three times.

sentences.zh: '爾等能如曾之省身，則何過之有？」
