translations.literal: If you could examine yourselves as Zeng did, what fault would there be?"
translations.idiomatic: If you examined yourselves as Zeng did, what fault would remain?"

sentences.zh: 旋命固山額真石廷柱、馬光遠與諸漢官會鞫，坐世昌死。

translations.literal: Soon he ordered gusa ejen Shi Tingzhu and Ma Guangyuan to join with Han officials in joint trial; Shichang was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered gusa commanders Shi Tingzhu and Ma Guangyuan to try Shichang with Han officials; Shichang was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 其弟世廕同居，知其事，啟心郎孫應時為改疏稿，皆死。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shiyin lived with him and knew of the affair; qixinlang Sun Yingshi had altered the memorial draft—all were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shiyin knew; Sun Yingshi had altered the draft—all were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 禮部承政甲喇章京姜新、甲喇章京馬光先見疏稿稱善，當奪職坐罰。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites jalan zhangjing Jiang Xin and jalan zhangjing Ma Guangxian had praised the draft as good and should have been stripped of office and fined.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xin and Ma Guangxian had praised the draft and should have been stripped and fined.

sentences.zh: 上命誅應時，而貸世昌、世廕，徙邊外席北。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Yingshi executed but spared Shichang and Shiyin, exiling them beyond the frontier to Xibei.
translations.idiomatic: The khan executed Yingshi but spared Shichang and Shiyin, exiling them to Xibei beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 新解承政，與光先皆貰罪。

translations.literal: Jiang Xin was relieved of his ministerial post; he and Guangxian were both fined.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xin was removed from office; he and Guangxian were fined.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，召還，隸漢軍鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he was recalled and enrolled in the Han Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 2 he was recalled and placed in the Han Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，授右副都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, seventh month, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 時盜發盂、五台、永寧、靜樂諸縣，世昌遣兵捕治。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in Yu, Wutai, Yongning, Jingle, and other counties; Shichang dispatched troops to capture and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in Yu, Wutai, Yongning, Jingle, and other counties; Shichang sent troops against them.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，上遣英親王阿濟格等戍大同備邊，總兵官姜瓖疑見誅，遂叛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year the sovereign dispatched Prince Ying Ajige and others to garrison Datong on frontier defense; Regional Commander Jiang Xiang, suspecting he would be executed, then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, twelfth month, Prince Ying Ajige was sent to garrison Datong; Regional Commander Jiang Xiang, fearing execution, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 世昌檄諸縣兵還守省城，瓖遣兵陷朔州、岢嵐，攻代州急，世昌帥師赴援，疏請發禁旅出居庸取大同，分兵出紫荊關，至代州濟師。

translations.literal: Shichang ordered the county troops back to defend the provincial capital; Xiang sent troops to take Shuozhou and Kelan and pressed the attack on Daizhou urgently; Shichang led troops to relieve the siege and memorialized requesting banner troops out through Juyong to take Datong, divided troops out through Zijing Pass, and reach Daizhou to succor the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang recalled county troops to defend Taiyuan; Xiang took Shuozhou and Kelan and pressed Daizhou; Shichang marched to relieve the city and asked for banner troops through Juyong against Datong and through Zijing Pass to reinforce Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 上命阿濟格等討瓖，別遣敬謹親王尼堪等帥師鎮太原。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Ajige and others to attack Xiang and separately dispatched Prince Jinggiyan Nikan and others to garrison Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ajige against Xiang and sent Prince Jinggiyan Nikan to hold Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，瓖將姚舉等掠平原驛，戕冀寧道王昌齡，下忻州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year Xiang's generals Yao Ju and others plundered Pingyuan Post, killed Jining Circuit Intendant Wang Changling, and descended on Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, first month, Xiang's generals Yao Ju and others raided Pingyuan Post, killed intendant Wang Changling, and attacked Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 固山額真庫魯克、達爾漢、阿賴等破舉眾石嶺關，舉棄忻州走。

translations.literal: Gusa ejen Kuluk, Darhan, Alai, and others broke Ju's host at Shiling Pass; Ju abandoned Xinzhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gusa commanders Kuluk, Darhan, and Alai routed Ju at Shiling Pass; Ju fled Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 既，复襲陷寧武，萬鍊踞偏關，劉遷破繁峙、靜樂及交城東關。

translations.literal: Before long they again raided and took Ningwu; Wan Lian held Pianguan and Liu Qian broke Fanzhi, Jingle, and the east gate of Jiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they took Ningwu again; Wan Lian held Pianguan and Liu Qian seized Fanzhi, Jingle, and Jiaocheng's east gate.

sentences.zh: 世昌疏趣援，尼堪師至，出攻寧武，踰月未下，移師向大同。

translations.literal: Shichang memorialized urging relief; when Nikan's army arrived it attacked Ningwu but could not take it in more than a month and shifted troops toward Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang urged relief; Nikan besieged Ningwu for a month without success and marched toward Datong.

sentences.zh: 瓖黨以其間攻陷保德、交城、石樓、永和諸縣，世昌復請發禁旅守太原、曲沃。

translations.literal: Xiang's followers in the interval attacked and took Baode, Jiaocheng, Shilou, Yonghe, and other counties; Shichang again requested banner troops to guard Taiyuan and Quwo.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's men meanwhile took Baode, Jiaocheng, Shilou, Yonghe, and other counties; Shichang again asked for banner troops at Taiyuan and Quwo.

sentences.zh: 李建泰以大學士罷歸，謀應瓖叛，世昌得其手書以聞。

translations.literal: Li Jiantai, dismissed from office as grand secretary and returning home, plotted to join Xiang in rebellion; Shichang obtained his letter in his own hand and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Jiantai, returning home after dismissal, plotted with Xiang; Shichang seized his letter and reported it.

sentences.zh: 會瓖為其將楊振威所殺，以大同降，師討定汾、絳、潞安、永寧、寧鄉諸州縣。

translations.literal: Just then Xiang was killed by his general Yang Zhenwei, who surrendered Datong; the army pacified Fen, Jiang, Lu'an, Yongning, Ningxiang, and other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was then killed by his general Yang Zhenwei, who surrendered Datong; the army pacified Fen, Jiang, Lu'an, Yongning, Ningxiang, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 建泰與瓖將李大猷等入太平，師從之，建泰等亦降。

translations.literal: Jiantai with Xiang's general Li Dayou and others entered Taiping; the army followed them and Jiantai and the others also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantai and Xiang's general Li Dayou entered Taiping; when the army arrived, they too surrendered.

sentences.zh: 是歲平陽盜虞允、韓昭宣為亂，攻陷州縣，應瓖，陝西總督孟喬芳將兵擊破之，世昌以聞。

translations.literal: That year the Pingyang bandits Yu Yun and Han Zhaoxuan made trouble, attacked and seized prefectures and counties, and answered Xiang; Shaanxi Governor-General Meng Qiaofang led troops to defeat them, and Shichang reported it.
translations.idiomatic: That year Pingyang bandits Yu Yun and Han Zhaoxuan rebelled, seized counties, and aided Xiang; Shaanxi governor-general Meng Qiaofang defeated them, as Shichang reported.

sentences.zh: 山西底定。

translations.literal: Shanxi was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，諡僖靖。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died and was given the posthumous title Xijing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year and was posthumously titled Xijing.

sentences.zh: 天聰間，有徐明遠者，疏陳時事，因言：「軍中得良家婦，上悉令歸故夫。

translations.literal: During the Tiancong period there was Xu Mingyuan, who memorialized on current affairs and said: "In the army when women of good families are taken, Your Majesty orders them all returned to their former husbands.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancong era Xu Mingyuan wrote on current affairs: "When women of good families are taken in the army, Your Majesty orders them returned to their husbands.

sentences.zh: 此誠如天之仁，禹、湯、文、武殆莫能過。

translations.literal: This is truly benevolence like Heaven's; Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu could scarcely surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly heaven-like benevolence—greater than Yu, Tang, Wen, or Wu.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見遵化、永平俘得良家婦，其主貪利，輒鬻入樂戶，得無損上仁聲？

translations.literal: Your servant has seen that in Zunhua and Yongping, when captive women of good families are obtained, their masters, greedy for profit, sell them into music households—will this not harm Your Majesty's reputation for benevolence?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Zunhua and Yongping, masters sell captive women of good families to music households for profit—does that not tarnish your benevolent name?

sentences.zh: 且樂戶既多，吏民遊冶，損財物，耗精血，於國無益。

translations.literal: Moreover, with many music households, officials and commoners indulge in pleasure, wasting goods and draining vital energy—to the state's no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Many music households lead officials and people into dissipation, wasting wealth and strength without benefit to the state.

sentences.zh: 買良為賤，古著於令甲，今豈可任其所為而不之禁乎？」

translations.literal: Buying the good to make them base is forbidden in ancient statutes—how can their deeds be left unchecked today?"
translations.idiomatic: Buying decent people into servitude was forbidden in ancient law—how can it be left unchecked now?"

sentences.zh: 明遠蓋自永平降者，事互見張存仁傳。

translations.literal: Mingyuan had himself surrendered from Yongping; the affair is also treated in Zhang Cunren's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan had surrendered from Yongping; the affair is also noted in Zhang Cunren's biography.

sentences.zh: 世昌繼以為言，乃得罪。

translations.literal: Shichang later spoke similarly and therefore incurred guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang spoke similarly later and was punished for it.

sentences.zh: 論曰：順治初，諸督撫多自文館出。

translations.literal: Commentary says: In early Shunzhi most governors-general and grand coordinators came from the Literary Institute.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: In early Shunzhi most governors came from the Literary Institute.

sentences.zh: 蓋國方新造，用滿臣與民閡，用漢臣又與政地閡，惟文館諸臣本為漢人，而侍直既久，情事相浹，政令皆習聞，為最宜也。

translations.literal: The state was newly founded; employing Manchu ministers estranged them from the people, and employing Han ministers estranged them from power—only institute scholars, being Han, yet serving in attendance for long, shared intimate knowledge of affairs and were accustomed to hearing government orders, and were therefore most suitable.
translations.idiomatic: The new dynasty could not rely on Manchu ministers alone, who stood apart from the people, nor on Han ministers alone, who stood apart from power; institute scholars, Han yet long in attendance, knew the business of government and were best suited to rule.

sentences.zh: 文盛、世昌未嘗直文館，而自太祖朝已來附，抒讜效忱，遂與文奎、棲鳳、國柱輩分領疆圻，各著聲績。

translations.literal: Wensheng and Shichang had never served in the institute, yet submitted from the Taizu Emperor's time onward, offered loyal counsel, and thus with Wenkui, Qifeng, Guozhu, and the others divided the frontier, each achieving renown.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng and Shichang never served in the institute, yet had submitted since the Taizu Emperor's day, offered loyal counsel, and with Wenkui, Qifeng, and Guozhu governed the frontiers with distinction.

sentences.zh: 天聰間諸言時政者，並以類附見。

translations.literal: Those who spoke on current affairs in the Tiancong period are all appended here by category.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists on current affairs in the Tiancong era are appended here by category.

sentences.zh: 當時章奏，流傳蓋鮮，經綸草昧，毋俾終湮也。

translations.literal: Memorials of that time are rarely transmitted; in the founding of policy let them not be lost to oblivion.
translations.idiomatic: Few memorials of that time survive; in those founding years of statecraft, let them not be lost.
